knowledge_statements.title: One-Norm Budget Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional epigraph representation of an affine one-norm budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an affine residual \(r(x)=Ax-b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and a budget \(\rho\ge 0\), the constraint \(\lVert r(x)\rVert_1\le \rho\) is convex. It holds if and only if there exists \(t\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \(-t_i\le r_i(x)\le t_i\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(t_i\ge 0\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^m t_i\le\rho\). Thus an affine one-norm budget has an exact linear-inequality formulation using componentwise magnitude variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine one-norm budget is exactly representable by nonnegative variables bounding each absolute residual and one linear constraint on their sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Ax-b\rVert_1\le\rho\iff\exists t\ge0:\ -t\le Ax-b\le t,\ \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}t\le\rho\)

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Ball Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order-cone representation of a finite-dimensional Euclidean ball constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=Ax-b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) be affine and let \(\rho\ge0\). The Euclidean-ball constraint \(\lVert r(x)\rVert_2\le\rho\) is equivalent to membership \((\rho,r(x))\in\mathcal{Q}_{m+1}\), where \(\mathcal{Q}_{m+1}=\{(s,z)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^m:\lVert z\rVert_2\le s\}\). Hence its feasible set is convex and the constraint is directly representable by one second-order cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine Euclidean-ball constraint is exactly one second-order-cone membership constraint and therefore defines a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2\le\rho\iff(\rho,Ax-b)\in\mathcal{Q}_{m+1}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Infinity-Norm Box Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear representation of an affine infinity-norm ball as a coordinate box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r(x)=Ax-b\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(\rho\ge0\), the constraint \(\lVert r(x)\rVert_\infty\le\rho\) holds exactly when \(-\rho\le r_i(x)\le\rho\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Equivalently, \(-\rho\mathbf{1}\le Ax-b\le\rho\mathbf{1}\) componentwise. The feasible residuals form the axis-aligned box \([-\rho,\rho]^m\), so an affine infinity-norm constraint is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinity-norm bound is exactly a pair of linear bounds on every residual coordinate, producing an axis-aligned box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Ax-b\rVert_\infty\le\rho\iff-\rho\mathbf{1}\le Ax-b\le\rho\mathbf{1}\)

notation.meaning: all-ones vector in the residual space

knowledge_statements.title: General p-Norm Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine vector constraints for the full range \(1\le p\le\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in[1,\infty)\), define \(\lVert z\rVert_p=(\sum_{i=1}^m|z_i|^p)^{1/p}\), and define \(\lVert z\rVert_\infty=\max_i|z_i|\). A general affine \(p\)-norm constraint is \(\lVert Ax-b\rVert_p\le\rho\), with \(\rho\ge0\). Because every \(p\)-norm in this range is convex and composition with an affine map preserves convexity, its feasible set \(\{x:\lVert Ax-b\rVert_p\le\rho\}\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general p-norm constraint bounds an affine residual in a norm with p between one and infinity and always defines a convex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\lVert Ax-b\rVert_p\le\rho\}\text{ is convex}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Norm Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal and linear-map weightings of finite-dimensional vector norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times m}\), let \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) be a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^k\), and let \(r(x)=Ax-b\). The weighted constraint \(\lVert Wr(x)\rVert\le\rho\) is convex for \(\rho\ge0\). If \(W\) is injective, then \(z\mapsto\lVert Wz\rVert\) is a norm; otherwise it is a seminorm. For diagonal \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w)\) with \(w_i>0\), this template assigns positive coordinate weights and defines the unit ball \(\{z:\lVert Wz\rVert\le1\}=W^{-1}\{u:\lVert u\rVert\le1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying a linear weighting before a norm yields a convex constraint; it is a genuine norm exactly when the weighting map is injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert W(Ax-b)\rVert\le\rho\text{ is convex, and }\lVert W\cdot\rVert\text{ is a norm iff }\ker W=\{0\}\)

children.title: Block-Separable Norm Constraints
children.top_down_role: Constraints organized by separable norm blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Norm Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraints separated across a fixed partition of the residual coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition an affine residual as \(r(x)=(r_1(x),\ldots,r_G(x))\), where \(r_g(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m_g}\), and choose norms \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{(g)}\) with budgets \(\rho_g\ge0\). A block-separable norm constraint is the family \(\lVert r_g(x)\rVert_{(g)}\le\rho_g\) for every \(g=1,\ldots,G\). Its feasible set is the intersection of the blockwise inverse images of norm balls and is therefore convex. No inequality in this representation combines residual coordinates belonging to distinct blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-separable constraints impose an independent norm budget on each residual block; their joint feasible set is the intersection of convex block constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F=\bigcap_{g=1}^G\{x:\lVert r_g(x)\rVert_{(g)}\le\rho_g\}\text{ is convex}\)

children.title: Mixed-Norm Constraint Families
children.top_down_role: Nested norm families across grouped variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Norm Constraint Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested block norms with an outer aggregation exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_G)\) be partitioned into blocks, let \(q_g\in[1,\infty]\), and let \(p\in[1,\infty]\). The mixed norm is \(\lVert z\rVert_{p,(q_g)}=\lVert(\lVert z_1\rVert_{q_1},\ldots,\lVert z_G\rVert_{q_G})\rVert_p\). A mixed-norm constraint has the form \(\lVert r(x)\rVert_{p,(q_g)}\le\rho\), where \(r\) is affine and \(\rho\ge0\). This function is a norm, and its affine sublevel set is convex; the outer norm couples the block magnitudes through one shared budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed norm first measures each block and then aggregates those magnitudes with an outer norm, creating one convex shared-budget constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r(x)\rVert_{p,(q_g)}\le\rho\text{ defines a convex feasible set}\)

children.title: Cross-Block Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural coupling between otherwise distinct norm blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Coupling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A separability criterion in block-magnitude space for constraints built from block norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_g(x)=\lVert r_g(x)\rVert_{(g)}\) and \(u(x)=(u_1(x),\ldots,u_G(x))\), where each \(r_g\) is affine. If \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}_+^G\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and coordinatewise nondecreasing, then \(\Phi(u(x))\le\rho\) is a convex constraint. Define this constraint to be block-separable in magnitude space when there exist sets \(S_g\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+\) such that \(\{u\in\mathbb{R}_+^G:\Phi(u)\le\rho\}=S_1\times\cdots\times S_G\). If no such factorization exists, the admissible block magnitudes are cross-block coupled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinatewise nondecreasing convex aggregator gives a convex constraint. The admissible magnitude set is block-separable exactly when it factors into one scalar set per block; otherwise the block magnitudes are coupled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi(u(x))\le\rho\text{ is separable in magnitude space}\iff\{u\in\mathbb{R}_+^G:\Phi(u)\le\rho\}=\prod_{g=1}^G S_g\text{ for some }S_g\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+\)

notation.meaning: admissible scalar magnitudes for block g

children.title: Block-Norm Conic Representation Routes
children.top_down_role: Conic representation choices for structured block norms.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Norm Conic Representation Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph lifting of mixed block norms into inner and outer cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block residuals \(r_g(x)\), introduce \(t_g\ge0\). The mixed-norm constraint \(\lVert(\lVert r_1(x)\rVert_{q_1},\ldots,\lVert r_G(x)\rVert_{q_G})\rVert_p\le\rho\) is equivalent to the existence of \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_G)\) satisfying \(\lVert r_g(x)\rVert_{q_g}\le t_g\) for every \(g\) and \(\lVert t\rVert_p\le\rho\). Consequently, whenever each inner norm epigraph and the outer \(p\)-norm ball have representations over chosen cones, their conjunction gives an exact lifted conic representation of the block constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift each block magnitude into an auxiliary variable, represent the inner norm bounds, then constrain the auxiliary vector by the outer norm cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert(\lVert r_g(x)\rVert_{q_g})_{g=1}^G\rVert_p\le\rho\iff\exists t\ge0:\ \lVert r_g(x)\rVert_{q_g}\le t_g\ \forall g,\ \lVert t\rVert_p\le\rho\)

notation.meaning: lifted upper bound for block g's norm
inner norm exponent for block g

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Induced Norm Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraints using the norm of a linear operator between normed finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^k\) be linear, with norms \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathrm{in}}\) and \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathrm{out}}\). Its induced operator norm is \(\lVert T\rVert_{\mathrm{in}\to\mathrm{out}}=\sup_{z\ne0}\lVert Tz\rVert_{\mathrm{out}}/\lVert z\rVert_{\mathrm{in}}\). An operator-induced norm constraint is \(\lVert T(x)\rVert_{\mathrm{in}\to\mathrm{out}}\le\rho\) when \(T(x)\) depends affinely on decision variables. It asserts \(\lVert T(x)z\rVert_{\mathrm{out}}\le\rho\lVert z\rVert_{\mathrm{in}}\) for every \(z\), and its tractable conic form depends on the chosen norm pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An induced-norm constraint uniformly bounds an affine decision-dependent operator's output over all inputs, relative to specified input and output norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert T(x)\rVert_{\mathrm{in}\to\mathrm{out}}\le\rho\iff\lVert T(x)z\rVert_{\mathrm{out}}\le\rho\lVert z\rVert_{\mathrm{in}}\ \forall z\in\mathbb{R}^m\)

notation.meaning: operator norm induced by the input and output norms

children.title: Gauge-Based Constraints
children.top_down_role: Constraint templates built from convex gauges.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Based Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski-functional constraints generated by closed convex sets containing the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be closed and convex, contain \(0\), and be absorbing. Its gauge is \(\gamma_C(z)=\inf\{\lambda\ge0:z\in\lambda C\}\). The gauge is nonnegative, convex, and positively homogeneous, but need not satisfy \(\gamma_C(z)=\gamma_C(-z)\). For an affine residual \(r(x)\) and \(\rho>0\), the gauge constraint \(\gamma_C(r(x))\le\rho\) is equivalent to \(r(x)\in\rho C\), and hence defines a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge measures the scaling needed to place a vector in a convex reference set; its sublevel constraint is scaled-set membership.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is closed, convex, absorbing, and }0\in C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(r(x))\le\rho\iff r(x)\in\rho C\)

notation.meaning: convex reference set defining the gauge

children.title: Asymmetric Convex Constraints
children.top_down_role: Directional constraint families lacking central symmetry.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric Convex Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex directional constraints generated by non-even sublinear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^m\to[0,\infty)\) be finite and sublinear, without requiring evenness. For an affine map \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(\rho\ge0\), the constraint \(\phi(r(x))\le\rho\) is convex. It is directionally asymmetric when some \(z\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies \(\phi(z)\ne\phi(-z)\), and its residual sublevel sets are then not required to be centrally symmetric. If \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is closed, convex, absorbing, and contains \(0\), its finite gauge \(\gamma_C\) is even if and only if \(C=-C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-even sublinear function yields a convex but directionally asymmetric constraint. For a closed convex absorbing gauge set containing the origin, the gauge is symmetric exactly when the set is centrally symmetric.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is closed, convex, absorbing, and }0\in C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:\phi(r(x))\le\rho\}\text{ is convex, and }\gamma_C(z)=\gamma_C(-z)\ \forall z\iff C=-C\)

notation.meaning: closed convex set generating the gauge

children.title: Polar-Gauge Geometry
children.top_down_role: Polar geometry associated with gauge-based constraint sets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C=\sigma_{C^\circ}\), \(\gamma_{C^\circ}=\sigma_C\), and \(\langle y,x\rangle\leq\gamma_C(x)\gamma_{C^\circ}(y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional compact convex bodies; symmetry is not assumed.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Geometry of the primal and dual problems p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t>0:x\in tC\}\), \(C^\circ=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle y,z\rangle\leq1\text{ for every }z\in C\}\), and \(\sigma_C(y)=\sup_{z\in C}\langle y,z\rangle\). Then, for every \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\gamma_C(x)=\sigma_{C^\circ}(x)\), \(\gamma_{C^\circ}(y)=\sigma_C(y)\), and \(\langle y,x\rangle\leq\gamma_C(x)\gamma_{C^\circ}(y)\). These identities do not require \(C=-C\), and the two gauges need not be even functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact convex body containing the origin in its interior, the gauge is the support function of the polar, the polar gauge is the original body's support function, and the resulting generalized Hölder inequality does not require symmetry.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Gauge Geometry

children.title: Symmetrization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of replacing asymmetric geometry with symmetric norm models.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and convex, \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\), and \(C\) contains no affine line.
\(\alpha_C=\inf\{\alpha\geq1:-C\subseteq\alpha C\}\), with the infimum interpreted as \(+\infty\) if the set is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C(x)\leq\gamma_{C\cap(-C)}(x)\leq\alpha_C\gamma_C(x)\) when \(\alpha_C<\infty\); no finite uniform factor of this form exists when \(\alpha_C=+infty\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: gauge order reversal and the definition of the symmetry coefficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-free closed convex sets with the origin in their interior; quantifies the boundary for replacing an asymmetric gauge by the norm induced by inner symmetrization.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Geometry of the primal and dual problems p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\gamma_{C\cap(-C)}(x)=\max\{\gamma_C(x),\gamma_C(-x)\}\), and \(\gamma_{C\cap(-C)}\) is a norm. If \(\alpha_C<\infty\), then \(\gamma_C(x)\leq\gamma_{C\cap(-C)}(x)\leq\alpha_C\gamma_C(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The gauge \(\gamma_C\) is itself a norm exactly when \(C=-C\). If \(\alpha_C=+\infty\), there is no finite constant \(K\) such that \(\gamma_{C\cap(-C)}(x)\leq K\gamma_C(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a line-free asymmetric convex set, inner symmetrization produces a norm. Its distortion relative to the original gauge is bounded exactly when the symmetry coefficient is finite, while the original gauge is already a norm exactly in the centrally symmetric case.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetrization Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Frobenius norm satisfies \(\|X\|_F=\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n X_{ij}^2\bigr)^{1/2}=\|\operatorname{vec}X\|_2\). Feasibility necessarily implies \(t\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Frobenius-norm bound is exactly a Lorentz-cone constraint on the vectorized matrix and its scalar bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The spectral-norm epigraph has the semidefinite representation \[\|X\|_2\leq t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\begin{pmatrix}tI_m&X\\X^\top&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Equivalently, for \(t\geq0\), the Schur-complement condition is \(XX^\top\preceq t^2I_m\), or equivalently \(X^\top X\preceq t^2I_n\). Thus an affine spectral-norm constraint remains a linear matrix inequality after substituting the affine matrix expression for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounding a matrix's largest singular value is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of a symmetric block matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nuclear-norm constraint \(\|X\|_*\leq t\) holds if and only if there exist symmetric matrices \(W\in\mathbb{S}^m\) and \(Z\in\mathbb{S}^n\) such that \[\begin{pmatrix}W&X\\X^\top&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad \frac{1}{2}\bigl(\operatorname{tr}W+\operatorname{tr}Z\bigr)\leq t.\] This lifted formulation is convex and exact; its feasibility also implies \(W\succeq0\), \(Z\succeq0\), and \(t\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nuclear-norm bound is exactly representable by a positive-semidefinite block matrix and a trace inequality using two lifted symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Nuclear-Norm Constraints

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the dual norm by \(\|y\|_*=\sup\{\langle y,x\rangle:x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \|x\|\leq1\}\). Then every \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(|\langle y,x\rangle|\leq\|x\|\|y\|_*\), and finite-dimensional biduality gives \(\|x\|=\sup\{\langle y,x\rangle:y\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \|y\|_*\leq1\}\). For conjugate exponents \(p,q\in[1,\infty]\) satisfying \(1/p+1/q=1\), with \(1/\infty=0\), the dual of \(\ell_p\) is \(\ell_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual norm is the maximum pairing over the primal unit ball, gives the generalized Hölder inequality, and recovers the primal norm by finite-dimensional biduality; conjugate l-p and l-q norms form the standard examples.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Norm Pairings

assumptions_latex: \(B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|x\|\leq1\}\) is the unit ball of a norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B^\circ=\{y:\|y\|_*\leq1\}\) and \((B^\circ)^\circ=B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar correspondence for closed norm balls in finite-dimensional real spaces.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Geometry of the primal and dual problems p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B=\{x:\|x\|\leq1\}\), define its polar by \(B^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\leq1\text{ for every }x\in B\}\). Then \(B^\circ=\{y:\|y\|_*\leq1\}\), so the polar of the primal unit ball is exactly the dual unit ball. Because \(B\) is closed, convex, and contains the origin, the bipolar identity gives \((B^\circ)^\circ=B\). Scaling yields \((rB)^\circ=r^{-1}B^\circ\) for every \(r>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar of a norm's unit ball is the dual-norm unit ball; taking the polar again recovers the original ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Ball Correspondence

assumptions_latex: \(B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|x\|\leq1\}\) is the unit ball of a norm.

notation.meaning: support function of a set C

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function identity used to eliminate norm-ball uncertainty.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Geometry of the primal and dual problems p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the support function of the norm unit ball is \[\sigma_B(y)=\sup_{x\in B}\langle y,x\rangle=\|y\|_*.\] More generally, positive homogeneity gives \(\sigma_{rB}(y)=r\|y\|_*\). Therefore an inequality required for every perturbation \(u\in rB\) can replace the worst-case linear term \(\sup_{u\in rB}\langle y,u\rangle\) by the deterministic expression \(r\|y\|_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a norm ball is the radius times the dual norm, converting worst-case linear perturbations into deterministic norm terms.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Functions of Norm Balls

knowledge_statements.title: Right-Hand-Side Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact robust counterpart for uncertainty confined to the right-hand side of scalar inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), and consider \(a_i(x)\le b_i(u)\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\), where \(a_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is deterministic. Its robust counterpart is
\[
a_i(x)\le \inf_{u\in\mathcal U}b_i(u).
\]
If \(b_i(u)=\bar b_i+d_i^{\mathsf T}u\), then the same condition is
\[
a_i(x)-\bar b_i+\sigma_{\mathcal U}(-d_i)\le0,
\]
where \(\sigma_{\mathcal U}(z)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}z^{\mathsf T}u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint with only right-hand-side uncertainty is robust exactly when its deterministic left side does not exceed the smallest admissible right side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i(x)\le b_i(u)\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\iff a_i(x)\le\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}b_i(u)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Objective Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case interpretation of an uncertain objective over a prescribed uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), and let \(f:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). The robust objective associated with minimizing \(f(x,u)\) under uncertainty is
\[
F(x):=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}f(x,u).
\]
The robust optimization problem minimizes \(F(x)\) over the robust feasible set \(X_R\subseteq X\). Thus a decision is evaluated by its worst admissible objective value, while the same decision \(x\) must be selected before \(u\) is revealed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust objective uncertainty replaces each decision’s uncertain cost by its worst value over all admissible parameter realizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X_R}\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}f(x,u)\) is the static robust objective problem.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X_R\) and \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), \(t\ge F(x)\iff f(x,u)\le t\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), and let \(f:X_R\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). Define
\[
F(x):=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}f(x,u).
\]
Introducing \(t\in\mathbb{R}\) gives the extended-real equality
\[
\inf_{x\in X_R}F(x)=\inf_{x\in X_R,\,t\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{t:f(x,u)\le t\ \text{for every }u\in\mathcal U\right\}.
\]
For each fixed \(x\in X_R\), the infimum of the feasible values of \(t\) equals \(F(x)\). If \(X_R\) is convex and \(f(\cdot,u)\) is convex for every \(u\in\mathcal U\), then the resulting epigraph feasible set is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncertain worst-case objective is represented exactly by a real epigraph variable that upper-bounds every realized objective value.

children.title: Shared Epigraph Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coupling induced by epigraph variables shared across uncertain terms.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(J\) is finite and nonempty, and \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\) and \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), \(t\ge\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\max_{j\in J}f_j(x,u)\iff f_j(x,u)\le t\) for every \((j,u)\in J\times\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One epigraph variable jointly bounds all scenarios and objective components.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Robust optimization models p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(J\) be a nonempty finite index set, let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), and let \(f_j:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) for every \(j\in J\). Define
\[
F(x):=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\max_{j\in J}f_j(x,u).
\]
A shared epigraph variable \(t\in\mathbb{R}\) gives the exact representation
\[
t\ge F(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f_j(x,u)\le t\quad\text{for every }(j,u)\in J\times\mathcal U.
\]
An equivalent lifted system may use variables \(t_j\in\mathbb{R}\) together with \(f_j(x,u)\le t_j\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\) and \(t_j\le t\) for every \(j\in J\). Without a common upper bound \(t\), the separate variables do not represent the scalar epigraph of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared epigraph variable imposes one common worst-case bound across all objective components and uncertainty realizations; component-specific bounds are equivalent only when they are linked to that common bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared Epigraph Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Counterpart Tractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional tractability criterion for a robust objective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}f(x,u)\) over a convex robust feasible set. Its objective counterpart is tractable relative to a chosen conic class \(\mathcal K\) when the semi-infinite constraint
\[
f(x,u)\le t\quad\text{for all }u\in\mathcal U
\]
admits an exact finite representation \(G(x,t,y)\in\mathcal K\) using auxiliary variables \(y\) of polynomial encoding length, and membership and separation for \(\mathcal K\) are polynomial-time computable. Under these conditions, the robust objective adds only a polynomial-size conic formulation to the remaining robust constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust objective is tractable when its universal epigraph constraint has an exact polynomial-size representation in a computationally tractable cone.
assumptions_latex: The input data and uncertainty set have finite encodings.
The selected cone \(\mathcal K\) has polynomial-time membership and separation procedures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x,u)\le t\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\iff\exists y:\ G(x,t,y)\in\mathcal K\), with polynomial representation size.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Parameter Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine dependence of uncertain constraint data on a finite-dimensional parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_L)\in\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^L\). An uncertain scalar constraint has an affine parameter perturbation when its defining function can be written
\[
g(x,u)=g_0(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}u_\ell g_\ell(x),
\]
so robust feasibility requires \(g(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\). Equivalently,
\[
g_0(x)+\sigma_{\mathcal U}(g_1(x),\ldots,g_L(x))\le0.
\]
The functions \(g_\ell\) may be nonlinear in \(x\); affineness here concerns only the uncertain parameter \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine perturbation expresses uncertain constraint data as a nominal term plus a linear combination of fixed perturbation directions.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_\ell:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is defined on the decision domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x,u)=g_0(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}u_\ell g_\ell(x)\) is affine in \(u\).

notation.meaning: support function of the uncertainty set

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Nonlinear Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear parameter dependence decomposed into coordinate-wise perturbation terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_L)\in\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^L\). A scalar uncertain constraint has a separable nonlinear perturbation when
\[
g(x,u)=g_0(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\phi_\ell(x,u_\ell),
\]
where each term depends on only one uncertainty coordinate but may depend nonlinearly on that coordinate. Robust feasibility is the condition
\[
\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\left[g_0(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\phi_\ell(x,u_\ell)\right]\le0.
\]
If \(\mathcal U=\prod_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathcal U_\ell\), the supremum separates into the sum of the coordinate-wise suprema.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable nonlinear perturbation is a sum of nonlinear terms, each involving only one uncertainty coordinate; product uncertainty sets permit coordinate-wise maximization.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\phi_\ell(x,\cdot)\) is defined on the corresponding coordinate projection of \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\prod_\ell\mathcal U_\ell\Rightarrow\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}g(x,u)=g_0(x)+\sum_\ell\sup_{s\in\mathcal U_\ell}\phi_\ell(x,s)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Nonaffine Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonaffine uncertainty dependence that cannot be decomposed coordinate-wise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u\in\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^L\). A scalar uncertain constraint has a coupled nonaffine perturbation when
\[
g(x,u)=g_0(x)+\Phi(x,u),
\]
where \(u\mapsto\Phi(x,u)\) is nonaffine and is not representable, on \(\mathcal U\), as \(c(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\phi_\ell(x,u_\ell)\). Its robust counterpart is
\[
g_0(x)+\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\Phi(x,u)\le0.
\]
Thus evaluation generally requires a joint maximization over the full uncertainty vector, even when \(\mathcal U\) is a Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled nonaffine perturbation depends jointly and nonlinearly on several uncertainty coordinates, so its worst case generally requires joint maximization.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi(x,u)\) is defined for every \((x,u)\in X\times\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x,u)\le0\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\iff g_0(x)+\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\Phi(x,u)\le0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Wise Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent uncertainty set assigned to each robust constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider constraints indexed by \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Constraint-wise uncertainty assigns a separate parameter \(u_i\in\mathcal U_i\) to each constraint and defines robust feasibility by
\[
g_i(x,u_i)\le0\quad\text{for every }u_i\in\mathcal U_i,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.
\]
Equivalently, each row is robustified independently as \(\sup_{u_i\in\mathcal U_i}g_i(x,u_i)\le0\). The joint uncertainty set is the Cartesian product \(\prod_{i=1}^{m}\mathcal U_i\), with no restriction linking realizations belonging to different constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-wise uncertainty robustifies each constraint over its own uncertainty set, without restrictions linking uncertainty realizations across constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is robust feasible iff \(\sup_{u_i\in\mathcal U_i}g_i(x,u_i)\le0\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: uncertainty set local to constraint i

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(m\ge1\), let \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\), and let \(g_i:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Shared-parameter uncertainty means that one realization \(u\in\mathcal U\) enters all constraints. Robust feasibility requires

g_i(x,u)\le0\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\text{ and every }u\in\mathcal U.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint-Budget Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single deviation budget couples uncertainty assigned to multiple constraints or blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\), with \(u_i\in V_i\), and let \(\rho_i:V_i\to[0,+\infty]\) measure the deviation allocated to constraint \(i\). A joint-budget uncertainty set is
\[
\mathcal U_\Gamma:=\left\{u\in\prod_{i=1}^{m}V_i:\sum_{i=1}^{m}\rho_i(u_i)\le\Gamma\right\},
\]
where \(\Gamma\ge0\). Robust feasibility requires \(g_i(x,u_i)\le0\) for every \(i\) and every joint vector \(u\in\mathcal U_\Gamma\). The shared budget prevents all components from simultaneously attaining deviations whose total cost exceeds \(\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint-budget uncertainty couples constraint-specific deviations by requiring their aggregate deviation cost not to exceed one common budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_\Gamma=\{u\in\prod_iV_i:\sum_i\rho_i(u_i)\le\Gamma\}\) couples all uncertainty components through one budget.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraints share uncertainty within blocks while different blocks remain uncoupled.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Robust optimization models p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(m\ge1\), and partition \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) into nonempty blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_K\). For each \(k\), let \(\mathcal U_k\neq\varnothing\), and for every \(i\in I_k\), let \(g_i:X\times\mathcal U_k\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). Block-coupled uncertainty assigns one parameter \(u^{(k)}\in\mathcal U_k\) to every constraint in block \(I_k\), with joint set
\[
\mathcal U=\prod_{k=1}^{K}\mathcal U_k.
\]
Robust feasibility is
\[
g_i\bigl(x,u^{(k)}\bigr)\le0
\quad\text{for every }k\in\{1,\ldots,K\},\ i\in I_k,\text{ and }u^{(k)}\in\mathcal U_k.
\]
Thus uncertainty is shared within each block, while realizations from distinct blocks vary independently over their respective sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-coupled uncertainty shares one realization within each constraint block while allowing the realizations associated with different blocks to vary independently.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Coupled Uncertainty

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Constraint Budget Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a shared deviation budget coupling otherwise separate robust constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(X\) be a decision set, and, for each \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(Z_i\ne\varnothing\), \(f_i:X\times Z_i\to\mathbb R\), and \(\rho_i:Z_i\to\mathbb R_+\). For a total budget \(\Gamma\ge0\), define
\[\mathcal U_\Gamma=\left\{(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\in\prod_{i=1}^m Z_i:\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(z_i)\le\Gamma\right\}.\]
Cross-constraint budget allocation requires
\[f_i(x,z_i)\le0\quad\text{for every }i=1,\ldots,m\text{ and every }(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\in\mathcal U_\Gamma.\]
Thus the deviations affecting different constraints draw from one shared uncertainty budget rather than from independent budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common deviation budget couples all uncertain constraints: deviations assigned to different constraints must collectively remain within the total budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in X\) is robustly feasible exactly when \(f_i(x,z_i)\le0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and every \(z\in\mathcal U_\Gamma\).

notation.meaning: Budget consumed by the deviation affecting constraint i.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Induced Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States feasible-set monotonicity when a coupled joint uncertainty set is replaced by independent combinations of its projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,r\in\mathbb N\), let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(Z_i\ne\varnothing\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and let \(f_j:X\times\prod_{i=1}^m Z_i\to\mathbb R\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\). For a nonempty coupled set \(\mathcal U\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^m Z_i\), define
\[\widehat{\mathcal U}=\prod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{proj}_i(\mathcal U),\qquad F(V)=\{x\in X:f_j(x,z)\le0\text{ for every }z\in V\text{ and }j=1,\ldots,r\}.\]
Because \(\mathcal U\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal U}\),
\[F(\widehat{\mathcal U})\subseteq F(\mathcal U).\]
Thus discarding cross-block coupling and allowing every independent combination of projected deviations cannot enlarge the robust feasible set and can make it strictly smaller.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a coupled uncertainty set by the product of its block projections can introduce joint deviations absent from the original set, so the robust feasible set can only shrink and may shrink strictly.
assumptions_latex: Each constraint function may depend on the full joint uncertainty vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\prod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{proj}_i(\mathcal U))\subseteq F(\mathcal U)\).

notation.meaning: Projection of the joint uncertainty set onto block i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust feasibility set and robustness-analysis problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static decisions that must satisfy every constraint for every realization in the uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a base decision set \(\mathcal X\) and uncertainty set \(\mathbf\Delta\), the robust feasibility set is \[\mathcal X(\mathbf\Delta)=\left\{x\in\mathcal X\mid f_i(x,\Delta)\le 0\ \text{for every }\Delta\in\mathbf\Delta,\ i=1,\ldots,p\right\}.\] The robustness-analysis problem is to determine whether a given candidate decision \(x\) belongs to \(\mathcal X(\mathbf\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The robust feasibility set contains exactly the decisions in the base decision set that satisfy every constraint under every allowed uncertainty realization. Robustness analysis checks membership of a candidate decision in this set.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal X\text{ is the base decision set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\mathcal X(\mathbf\Delta)\iff \left(x\in\mathcal X\ \land\ \forall\Delta\in\mathbf\Delta\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,p\},\ f_i(x,\Delta)\le 0\right).

children.title: Static Decision Commitment
children.top_down_role: Decision commitment before uncertain parameters are observed.

knowledge_statements.title: Static Decision Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines commitment to one uncertainty-independent decision in a robust model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\ne\varnothing\) be a decision set, let \(\mathcal U\ne\varnothing\) be an uncertainty set, and let \(f_j:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb R\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), where \(m\in\mathbb N\). A static decision commitment is a single vector \(x\in X\) selected without dependence on \(u\in\mathcal U\). Equivalently, if decisions are represented by policies \(\pi:\mathcal U\to X\), static commitment restricts the admissible policy class to
\[\Pi_{\mathrm{stat}}=\{\pi:\mathcal U\to X:\exists x\in X\text{ such that }\pi(u)=x\text{ for every }u\in\mathcal U\}.\]
Robust feasibility requires this same \(x\) to satisfy \(f_j(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\) and every \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static commitment selects one decision without using the uncertainty realization and uses that identical decision under every realization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{stat}}\) if and only if \(\pi\) is constant on \(\mathcal U\).

notation.meaning: Class of static, constant decision rules.

children.title: Pre-Uncertainty Decision Timing
children.top_down_role: Information timing associated with static robust decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Pre-Uncertainty Decision Timing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes the information restriction imposed when decisions precede uncertainty revelation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U\ne\varnothing\) be an uncertainty set, let \(X\ne\varnothing\) be a decision set, and let \(\mathcal P_0\) be the partition of \(\mathcal U\) induced by the information available when a policy \(x:\mathcal U\to X\) is chosen. Admissibility requires
\[u\text{ and }v\text{ lie in the same cell of }\mathcal P_0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x(u)=x(v).\]
If the decision is made before any uncertainty is revealed, then \(\mathcal P_0=\{\mathcal U\}\), and the condition becomes
\[x(u)=x(v)\quad\text{for all }u,v\in\mathcal U.\]
Consequently, every realization is evaluated using one common decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy may distinguish only realizations separated by information already available at decision time. Before any uncertainty is revealed, it must be constant across all realizations.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_0\) represents exactly the information available when the decision is chosen.
For the fully pre-uncertainty case, \(\mathcal P_0=\{\mathcal U\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathcal P_0=\{\mathcal U\}\), then \(x(u)=x(v)\) for all \(u,v\in\mathcal U\).

notation.meaning: Information partition available at the decision time.
Decision policy indexed by the uncertainty realization.

children.title: Nonadjustable Policy Scope
children.top_down_role: Policy classes restricted to uncertainty-independent choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonadjustable Policy Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies which decision components are forbidden from adapting to uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\in\mathbb N\), let \(\mathcal U\ne\varnothing\), let \(X_k\ne\varnothing\) for \(k=1,\ldots,p\), and let \(\pi:\mathcal U\to\prod_{k=1}^pX_k\) have components \(\pi(u)=(x_1(u),\ldots,x_p(u))\). For an index set \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\), the components in \(S\) are nonadjustable when
\[x_k(u)=x_k(v)\quad\text{for every }k\in S\text{ and all }u,v\in\mathcal U.\]
Equivalently, for every \(k\in S\), there exists \(\bar x_k\in X_k\) such that \(x_k(u)=\bar x_k\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\). Components outside \(S\) may depend on the information available when they are selected. Full static robustness is the special case \(S=\{1,\ldots,p\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonadjustable scope is the set of policy components required to remain identical under every uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy is nonadjustable on \(S\) exactly when each \(x_k\), \(k\in S\), is constant on \(\mathcal U\).

notation.meaning: Complete decision policy under realization u.
Feasible space for decision component k.

children.title: Recourse Exclusion Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary separating static decisions from recourse-enabled models.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Exclusion Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows how excluding post-observation recourse can destroy robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Static robustness restricts a recourse rule \(y:\mathcal U\to Y\) to be constant. This restriction can strictly reduce feasibility. For the concrete family
\[\mathcal U=\{-1,1\},\qquad Y=\mathbb R,\qquad y(u)=u,\]
interpreted as the pair of inequalities \(y(u)-u\le0\) and \(u-y(u)\le0\), the adjustable rule \(y(u)=u\) is feasible for every \(u\in\mathcal U\). No static value \(\bar y\) is feasible, because it would require simultaneously \(\bar y=-1\) and \(\bar y=1\). Thus the boundary is precisely the prohibition of uncertainty-dependent decisions after observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Excluding recourse may make a model infeasible even when a simple adjustable policy satisfies every realization; matching two distinct observed values is a minimal example.
assumptions_latex: The realization \(u\) is observable before an adjustable recourse decision would be made.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The adjustable model is feasible, whereas its constant-policy restriction is infeasible.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct two-scenario counterexample verifies the static-versus-adjustable feasibility boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Recourse Decision Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces from static robust models to post-observation decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Recourse Decision Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents robust decisions as here-and-now variables coupled to scenario-dependent recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in X\) be selected before uncertainty and let \(y(u)\in Y\) be selected after observing \(u\in\mathcal U\). A two-stage recourse interface represents robust feasibility as
\[x\in X,\qquad y\in\Pi,\qquad f_j(x,y(u),u)\le0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U\text{ and }j=1,\ldots,m,\]
where \(\Pi\subseteq Y^{\mathcal U}\) is the admissible policy class. The interface separates the committed decision \(x\), the information-responsive decision rule \(y\), and the constraints linking them under each realization. Any measurability or nonanticipativity requirement belongs to the definition of \(\Pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recourse interface couples one pre-uncertainty decision with an admissible post-observation decision rule and enforces every constraint for every realization.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\subseteq Y^{\mathcal U}\) specifies the permitted information dependence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust feasibility is equivalent to the existence of \(x\in X\) and \(y\in\Pi\) satisfying all realization-wise constraints.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard two-stage adjustable robust optimization quantifier structure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Adjustable Policy Classes
children.top_down_role: Policy families permitting dependence on revealed uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjustable Policy Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines common nested restrictions on uncertainty-responsive recourse rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) be nonempty. An adjustable policy is a map \(y:\mathcal U\to Y\). Define
\[\Pi_{\mathrm{stat}}=\{u\mapsto y_0:y_0\in Y\},\]
\[\Pi_{\mathrm{aff}}=\{u\mapsto y_0+Au:y_0\in\mathbb R^r,\ A\in\mathbb R^{r\times q},\ y_0+Au\in Y\text{ for every }u\in\mathcal U\},\]
and let \(\Pi_{\mathrm{meas}}\) be a specified class of measurable maps from \(\mathcal U\) to \(Y\). If \(\Pi_{\mathrm{meas}}\) contains every admissible affine map, then
\[\Pi_{\mathrm{stat}}\subseteq\Pi_{\mathrm{aff}}\subseteq\Pi_{\mathrm{meas}}.\]
Robust constraints are imposed only on policies belonging to the selected class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjustable policies may be restricted to constant, affine, or specified measurable rules. Under the stated inclusion convention, these classes are nested from least to most expressive.
assumptions_latex: The measurable-policy class contains every admissible affine map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_{\mathrm{stat}}\subseteq\Pi_{\mathrm{aff}}\subseteq\Pi_{\mathrm{meas}}\).

notation.meaning: Constant policies taking values in Y.
Affine policies taking values in Y on the uncertainty set.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard nested decision-rule classes in adjustable robust optimization

children.title: Information-Revelation Timing
children.top_down_role: Information structures governing when uncertainty becomes observable.

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Revelation Timing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States multistage nonanticipativity relative to revealed uncertainty histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\in\mathbb N\), let \(U_t\ne\varnothing\) and \(Y_t\ne\varnothing\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\), and let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\prod_{t=1}^T U_t\). For each \(t\), let \(y_t:\mathcal U\to Y_t\) be chosen after observing the history \(u_{1:t}=(u_1,\ldots,u_t)\). Information-revelation timing requires nonanticipativity:
\[u_{1:t}=v_{1:t}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y_t(u)=y_t(v)\qquad\text{for every }u,v\in\mathcal U\text{ and }t=1,\ldots,T.\]
Equivalently, for each \(t\), there is a map \(\phi_t\) on the set of attainable histories such that \(y_t(u)=\phi_t(u_{1:t})\). If the stage-\(t\) decision is made before \(u_t\) is revealed, the corresponding condition uses \(u_{1:t-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stage decision may depend only on uncertainty observed before that decision; scenarios with the same available history must receive the same decision.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\subseteq\prod_{t=1}^T U_t\) has a specified stagewise revelation order.
The observed history available to each decision stage is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t=1,\ldots,T\), \(y_t\) is nonanticipative exactly when it factors through the history available at stage \(t\).

notation.meaning: Uncertainty history observed through stage t.
Decision rule used at stage t.
Policy expressed as a function of the available history.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard nonanticipativity predicate for multistage policies

children.title: Static-to-Adjustable Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary between fixed robust decisions and adjustable formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Static-to-Adjustable Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes static robustness as the constant-policy restriction of adjustable robustness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Pi_1\subseteq\Pi_2\subseteq Y^{\mathcal U}\) be two recourse-policy classes and define
\[F(\Pi)=\{x\in X:\exists y\in\Pi\text{ such that }f_j(x,y(u),u)\le0\ \forall u\in\mathcal U,\ \forall j\}.\]
Then policy-class monotonicity gives \(F(\Pi_1)\subseteq F(\Pi_2)\). In particular, with \(\Pi_1=\Pi_{\mathrm{stat}}\) and \(\Pi_2=\Pi_{\mathrm{adj}}\), the static model is exactly the adjustable model restricted to constant policies, and
\[F(\Pi_{\mathrm{stat}})\subseteq F(\Pi_{\mathrm{adj}}).\]
For minimization with the same objective depending only on \(x\), the adjustable optimal value cannot exceed the static value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static robustness is adjustable robustness restricted to constant policies; permitting more responsive policies enlarges feasibility and cannot worsen a common minimization objective.
assumptions_latex: The compared models have identical uncertainty sets, constraints, and here-and-now objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\Pi_{\mathrm{stat}})\subseteq F(\Pi_{\mathrm{adj}})\), and \(v_{\mathrm{adj}}\le v_{\mathrm{stat}}\) for minimization.

notation.meaning: Here-and-now decisions feasible with policy class Pi.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct feasible-set monotonicity under nested policy classes
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Dependent Uncertainty Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines robust constraints whose admissible uncertainty realizations depend on the decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(U_0\) be an ambient uncertainty space, and let \(\mathcal U:X\rightrightarrows U_0\) be a nonempty-valued set mapping. A decision-dependent robust constraint has the form
\[f_j(x,u)\le0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U(x),\qquad j=1,\ldots,m.\]
Its robust feasible set is
\[F=\{x\in X:\sup_{u\in\mathcal U(x)}f_j(x,u)\le0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m\}.\]
Unlike exogenous uncertainty, both the tested realizations and constraint values may change with \(x\); convexity of each \(f_j(\cdot,u)\) alone therefore does not guarantee convexity of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision-dependent uncertainty assigns each decision its own uncertainty set, so feasibility tests both the decision and all realizations that decision activates.
assumptions_latex: Each supremum is interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F\) if and only if \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U(x)}f_j(x,u)\le0\) for every \(j\).

notation.meaning: Uncertainty set activated by decision x.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical set-valued formulation of endogenous uncertainty

knowledge_statements.title: Enumerated Scenario Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the finite constraint expansion for explicitly listed uncertainty scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the uncertainty set be the finite enumeration \(\mathcal U=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\), where repeated listed scenarios may be removed without changing the set. For constraint functions \(f_j:X\times\mathcal U\to\mathbb R\), the robust system
\[f_j(x,u)\le0\quad\text{for all }u\in\mathcal U\text{ and }j=1,\ldots,m\]
is equivalent to the finite deterministic family
\[f_j(x,u^s)\le0\quad\text{for }s=1,\ldots,N\text{ and }j=1,\ldots,m.\]
Thus an enumerated scenario set produces \(mN\) displayed scenario constraints before removal of duplicates or redundancies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely listed scenarios, robust feasibility is exactly feasibility of every constraint under every listed scenario.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is robustly feasible if and only if \(f_j(x,u^s)\le0\) for every pair \((j,s)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Hulls of Scenarios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario uncertainty represented by its convex hull for constraints affine in uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a set, let \(u^1,\ldots,u^N\in\mathbb R^m\), and define \[\mathcal U=\operatorname{conv}\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i u^i:\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i=1\right\}.\] Let \(g:X\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be such that \(u\mapsto g(x,u)\) is affine for every \(x\in X\). Then, for every \(x\in X\), \[g(x,u)\le0\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g(x,u^i)\le0\quad\text{for every }i=1,\ldots,N.\] Thus convexifying the finite scenario set does not change the robust feasible set for these uncertainty-affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every decision in the specified decision set, an uncertainty-affine inequality holds over finitely many scenarios exactly when it holds over their convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a set and \(g:X\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\).
For every \(x\in X\), the mapping \(u\mapsto g(x,u)\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\), \(g(x,u)\le0\) on \(\operatorname{conv}\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\) if and only if it holds at every supplied scenario.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scenario-Defined Perturbation Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario uncertainty-set geometry.

Given finitely many scenarios \(\zeta^{(1)},\ldots,\zeta^{(N)}\), a perturbation set \(\mathcal Z\) is scenario-defined if
\[
\mathcal Z=\operatorname{Conv}\{\zeta^{(1)},\ldots,\zeta^{(N)}\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perturbation set is scenario-defined if it is the convex hull of a given finite collection of scenarios.
assumptions_latex: \(\zeta^{(1)},\ldots,\zeta^{(N)}\) is a given finite family of scenarios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Z=\operatorname{Conv}\{\zeta^{(1)},\ldots,\zeta^{(N)}\}\).

children.title: Interval Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Componentwise lower-upper uncertainty descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent lower and upper bounds on scalar uncertain coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given bounds \(\ell_i,r_i\in\mathbb R\) with \(\ell_i\le r_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), interval uncertainty assigns each uncertain coordinate the interval \([\ell_i,r_i]\). The joint uncertainty set is the Cartesian product \[\mathcal U=\prod_{i=1}^m[\ell_i,r_i]=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\ell_i\le u_i\le r_i\ \text{for all }i\}.\] Equivalently, with \(c_i=(\ell_i+r_i)/2\) and \(d_i=(r_i-\ell_i)/2\), one has \(\mathcal U=\{c+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1\}\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each uncertain coordinate ranges independently between specified lower and upper bounds, producing a Cartesian product of intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\prod_{i=1}^m[\ell_i,r_i]=\{c+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1\}\).

notation.meaning: vectors of lower and upper coordinate bounds

children.title: Box Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Cartesian box geometries for multivariate uncertain parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Box Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Axis-aligned hyperrectangular uncertainty in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a center \(c\in\mathbb R^m\) and half-widths \(d\in\mathbb R_+^m\), the axis-aligned box uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U_{\mathrm{box}}=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:|u_i-c_i|\le d_i\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Writing \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d)\), it has the equivalent affine-image representation \[\mathcal U_{\mathrm{box}}=\{c+D z:z\in[-1,1]^m\}=\{c+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1\}.\] Zero half-widths are permitted and fix the corresponding coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box uncertainty set is an axis-aligned hyperrectangle specified by a center and nonnegative coordinate half-widths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{box}}=\{u:|u_i-c_i|\le d_i\}=\{c+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1\}\).

children.title: Coordinatewise Extremal Scenarios
children.top_down_role: Extreme scenarios induced by coordinatewise bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Extremal Scenarios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex reduction for maximizing an affine function over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U=\{c+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1\}\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d)\) and \(d\ge0\). For every \(a\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\max_{u\in\mathcal U}a^\top u=a^\top c+\sum_{i=1}^m d_i|a_i|=\max_{s\in\{-1,1\}^m}a^\top(c+D s).\] A maximizing vertex may be selected coordinatewise with \(s_i=1\) when \(a_i>0\), \(s_i=-1\) when \(a_i<0\), and either sign when \(a_i=0\). Consequently, a constraint affine in \(u\) is robust over the box exactly when it holds at all box vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine function reaches its box maximum at a vertex whose coordinates are chosen according to the coefficient signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{u\in\mathcal U}a^\top u=a^\top c+\sum_i d_i|a_i|\), attained at a coordinatewise extremal scenario.

notation.meaning: coefficient vector of the affine uncertain term

children.title: Correlation-Blindness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Modeling limits caused by absent dependence information.

knowledge_statements.title: Correlation-Blindness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservatism caused by replacing joint dependence information with coordinatewise intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Coordinatewise bounds do not encode dependence among uncertain coordinates. For example, let \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{corr}}=\{(t,t):|t|\le1\}\subset\mathbb R^2\). Its coordinatewise interval hull is \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{box}}=[-1,1]^2\). Although both sets have identical coordinate projections, \[\max_{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{corr}}}(u_1-u_2)=0,\qquad \max_{u\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{box}}}(u_1-u_2)=2.\] Hence replacing a dependent joint set by its coordinatewise box can strictly enlarge worst-case values and robust feasible-set restrictions; equality requires additional structure ensuring that the relevant box-extremal combinations are jointly attainable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginal intervals ignore dependence: their box may admit impossible coordinate combinations and yield strictly more conservative robust constraints.
assumptions_latex: The joint uncertainty set is replaced by the Cartesian product of its coordinate projections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Identical coordinate intervals need not imply identical worst-case affine values; the box replacement can be strictly conservative.

knowledge_statements.title: General Polyhedral Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncertainty sets represented by finitely many linear equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A general polyhedral uncertainty set in \(\mathbb R^m\) is a set admitting a representation \[\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:F u\le h,\ G u=q\},\] where \(F\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^r\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{s\times m}\), and \(q\in\mathbb R^s\); inequalities are componentwise. Equivalently, an affinely parameterized form is \(\mathcal U=\{u_0+Lz:Az\le b\}\). The set may be empty, unbounded, or lower-dimensional unless nonemptiness, boundedness, or full-dimensionality is imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General polyhedral uncertainty is described by finitely many linear inequalities and equalities, possibly through an affine parameterization.
assumptions_latex: All matrices and vectors have the displayed finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U\) is the solution set of finitely many affine equalities and componentwise affine inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Budgeted Polyhedral Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-normalized deviations constrained by a total deviation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^m\), deviation magnitudes \(d\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and budget \(\Gamma\in[0,m]\), the symmetric budgeted polyhedral uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U_\Gamma=\left\{\bar u+D z:|z_i|\le1\ \text{for all }i,\ \sum_{i=1}^m|z_i|\le\Gamma\right\},\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d).\] The budget limits aggregate normalized deviation while retaining individual coordinate bounds. In particular, \(\mathcal U_0=\{\bar u\}\), and \(\mathcal U_m=\{\bar u+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized coordinate deviations are individually bounded and their total absolute magnitude cannot exceed a prescribed budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U_\Gamma=\{\bar u+D z:\|z\|_\infty\le1,\ \|z\|_1\le\Gamma\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unstructured Norm-Bounded Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A full-dimensional perturbation ball with no prescribed directional or block structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^m\), let \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(\rho\ge0\). Unstructured norm-bounded uncertainty is the translated norm ball \[\mathcal U=\{\bar u+\delta:\delta\in\mathbb R^m,\ \|\delta\|\le\rho\}.\] The perturbation \(\delta\) may range over every direction in the ambient space; no sparsity, repeated-block, affine-subspace, or coupling restriction is imposed beyond the norm bound. For \(\rho>0\), the set is full-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uncertain vector may move from its nominal value in any direction, subject only to a norm-radius bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\bar u+\rho\{z\in\mathbb R^m:\|z\|\le1\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Norm-Bounded Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-bounded primitive disturbances mapped through a prescribed linear structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\), \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\rho\ge0\), and let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^k\). Structured norm-bounded uncertainty is \[\mathcal U=\{\bar u+Lz:z\in\mathbb R^k,\ \|z\|\le\rho\}.\] The fixed map \(L\) specifies allowable perturbation directions and their coupling. If \(L\) is rank deficient, then \(\mathcal U\) lies in the affine subspace \(\bar u+\operatorname{range}(L)\); if \(L\) is invertible, the set is a linearly transformed norm ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm-bounded primitive disturbance passes through a fixed linear map that encodes directions and coupling of uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on \(\mathbb R^k\) and \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\bar u+L\{z:\|z\|\le\rho\}\subseteq\bar u+\operatorname{range}(L)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Norm Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Grouped disturbances controlled through within-block and across-block norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(z\in\mathbb R^k\) into blocks \(z^{(1)},\ldots,z^{(B)}\). Given norms \(\|\cdot\|_{(b)}\) on the block spaces and an outer norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{out}}\) on \(\mathbb R^B\), define \[\mathcal Z=\left\{z:\left\|\bigl(\|z^{(1)}\|_{(1)},\ldots,\|z^{(B)}\|_{(B)}\bigr)\right\|_{\mathrm{out}}\le\rho\right\}.\] A block-norm uncertainty set is \(\mathcal U=\{\bar u+Lz:z\in\mathcal Z\}\). The inner norms measure block magnitudes, while the outer norm specifies how those magnitudes may combine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disturbances are partitioned into blocks; inner norms measure each block and an outer norm limits their combined magnitude.
assumptions_latex: The block spaces form a finite partition of \(\mathbb R^k\).
Every inner function and the outer function is a norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\bar u+L\mathcal Z\), where \(\mathcal Z\) is the unit ball of the stated composite block norm scaled by \(\rho\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact SDP representation of an ellipsoidally uncertain conic quadratic inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the associated semi-infinite conic quadratic inequality with ellipsoidal uncertainty; the referenced inequality (7.23) is not reproduced in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(m-1=\dim\zeta\ge 2\) and \(n=\dim b[x]\ge 3\). For the associated semi-infinite conic quadratic inequality with ellipsoidal uncertainty, \[x\text{ is feasible}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists X\in\mathcal L_{m,n}:\ \mathcal W\!\left([B[x],b[x]]\right)+X\succeq0.\] The displayed LMI has order \((n-1)(m-1)\) and gives an equivalent SDP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the uncertainty vector has dimension at least two and b(x) has dimension at least three, the associated ellipsoidally uncertain semi-infinite conic quadratic inequality is equivalent to the existence of a correction matrix X in L_{m,n} such that W([B(x),b(x)])+X is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ satisfies the associated semi-infinite uncertain CQI}\iff\exists X\in\mathcal L_{m,n}:\mathcal W([B[x],b[x]])+X\succeq0.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Ellipsoid Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nondegenerate ellipsoid centered at a nominal uncertain vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^m\), \(Q\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), and \(\rho>0\). A single nondegenerate ellipsoidal uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^m:(u-\bar u)^\top Q^{-1}(u-\bar u)\le\rho^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, for any nonsingular \(L\) satisfying \(Q=LL^\top\), \[\mathcal U=\{\bar u+Lz:\|z\|_2\le\rho\}.\] Positive definiteness of \(Q\) makes the ellipsoid bounded and full-dimensional; degeneracy is excluded from this local definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single ellipsoid is a translated, nonsingular linear image of a Euclidean ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U=\{u:(u-\bar u)^\top Q^{-1}(u-\bar u)\le\rho^2\}=\{\bar u+Lz:\|z\|_2\le\rho\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Intersections of Ellipsoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncertainty satisfying several simultaneous convex quadratic bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(j=1,\ldots,J\), let \(c_j\in\mathbb R^m\), \(Q_j\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\), and \(\rho_j>0\). An intersection-of-ellipsoids uncertainty set is \[\mathcal U=\bigcap_{j=1}^J\left\{u\in\mathbb R^m:(u-c_j)^\top Q_j^{-1}(u-c_j)\le\rho_j^2\right\}.\] It is closed and convex, and it is bounded whenever \(J\ge1\). It can be empty unless consistency is imposed. In general, the intersection need not itself be representable as one ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uncertain vector must satisfy multiple ellipsoidal inequalities simultaneously; the resulting convex set may be empty and is generally not one ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U\) is the closed convex intersection of the stated ellipsoids and need not be ellipsoidal or nonempty.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A degenerate ellipsoidal uncertainty set is an affine image
\[\mathcal U=\{\bar u+Pz:z\in\mathbb R^r,\ \|z\|_2\le 1\},\]
where \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\operatorname{rank}P<m\). It is contained in the proper affine subspace \(\bar u+\operatorname{range}P\). For every \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), its support function is
\[\sigma_{\mathcal U}(y)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}y^\top u=y^\top\bar u+\|P^\top y\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient affine image of the Euclidean unit ball is a lower-dimensional ellipsoid whose support function remains available in closed form.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is second-order-cone representable if there exist \(q\ge0\), finitely many affine maps, and an auxiliary vector \(z\in\mathbb R^q\) such that
\[U=\{u:\ \|A_i u+B_i z+a_i\|_2\le c_i^\top u+d_i^\top z+\beta_i\ \text{for all }i,\quad Eu+Fz=g\}.\]
The right-hand side of each cone inequality is thereby constrained to be nonnegative. Thus \(U\) is the projection onto the \(u\)-coordinates of an affine slice of a finite product of Lorentz cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is SOCP-representable when it is the projection of finitely many affine Lorentz-cone constraints and affine equalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone-Representable Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is semidefinite representable if there are symmetric matrices \(A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_m,B_1,\ldots,B_q\) of a common order such that
\[U=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\ \exists z\in\mathbb R^q,\ A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m u_iA_i+\sum_{j=1}^q z_jB_j\succeq0\right\}.\]
Equivalently, \(U\) is a linear projection of a spectrahedron. Such a set is convex; unlike a spectrahedron itself, its projection is not necessarily closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semidefinite-representable set is a projection of an affine positive-semidefinite matrix inequality; it is convex but may be nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite-Representable Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a closed convex cone. A lifted conic representation of \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is an identity
\[U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\ \exists z\in\mathbb R^q,\ Au+Bz+b\in K,\ Cu+Dz=d\}.\]
The lifted feasible set is the subset of \(\mathbb R^{m+q}\) satisfying the displayed conic and affine constraints; projecting it onto its first \(m\) coordinates yields exactly \(U\). Different lifts may represent the same uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted representation describes uncertainty using auxiliary variables and conic constraints whose projection onto the original coordinates equals the set.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Uncertainty Representations

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(V\subseteq\mathbb R^q\), a linear map \(T:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), the projected uncertainty set is
\[U=T(V)+b=\{Tv+b:v\in V\}.\]
Equivalently, \(U\) is the coordinate projection of \(\{(u,v):u=Tv+b,\ v\in V\}\). For every \(y\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[\sigma_U(y)=b^\top y+\sigma_V(T^\top y).\]
Convexity is preserved by this operation, while closedness need not be preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine image of a lifted uncertainty set is a projected uncertainty set; support directions pull back through the transpose map.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Uncertainty Sets

notation.meaning: Extension complexity relative to the cone family.

source_refs.locator: 6.4 Constructing Semidefinite Representations p. 271

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an admissible cone family \(\mathfrak K\) and an encoding convention assigning a nonnegative integer \(s(F)\) to each formulation \(F\). For a set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), its \(\mathfrak K\)-extension complexity is
\[\operatorname{xc}_{\mathfrak K}(U)=\inf\{s(F):F\text{ is an exact }\mathfrak K\text{-extended formulation whose projection is }U\}.\]
The size convention must account for the cone blocks and may also count auxiliary variables and affine equations. Consequently, sizes obtained under different cone families or encoding conventions are not directly comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extension complexity is the smallest encoded size of an exact lifted formulation, measured relative to a fixed cone family and counting convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Formulation Size

children.title: Projection Closure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Closure issues associated with projected uncertainty descriptions.

assumptions_latex: The lifted feasible set is closed and convex.
Projection is linear but no compactness or coercivity assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A linear projection of a closed convex conic set can fail to be closed.

notation.meaning: Projection onto the first two displayed coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit semidefinite projection showing failure of closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the closed convex cone
\[C=\left\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:\begin{pmatrix}x&y\\y&z\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb S_+^2\right\}.\]
Its projection onto \((x,y)\) is
\[\pi(C)=\{(x,y):x>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.\]
Indeed, when \(x>0\), choosing \(z\ge y^2/x\) gives positive semidefiniteness, whereas \(x=0\) forces \(y=0\). Hence \((1/k,1)\in\pi(C)\) converges to \((0,1)\notin\pi(C)\). Thus closedness of a lifted conic set alone does not ensure closedness of its projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed semidefinite cone slice can have a nonclosed projection; additional compactness or regularity is needed to guarantee projection closure.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Closure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit PSD-cone projection and its nonclosedness calculation are correct and the failure-boundary content kind is appropriate, but this nontrivial counterexample has no cited source or locator.

assumptions_latex: For fixed \(x\), the uncertain expression \(u\mapsto a(x)^\top u+b(x)\) is affine and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust inequality over \(U\), \(\operatorname{conv}U\), or \(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}U\) is equivalent.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector at the fixed decision.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar robust constraints affine in uncertainty.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Uncertain Linear Problems and their Robust Counterparts p. 32

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every fixed decision \(x\), let \(u\mapsto a(x)^\top u+b(x)\) be affine on \(\mathbb R^m\). Then
\[\sup_{u\in U}\bigl(a(x)^\top u+b(x)\bigr)=\sup_{u\in\operatorname{conv}U}\bigl(a(x)^\top u+b(x)\bigr)=\sup_{u\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}U}\bigl(a(x)^\top u+b(x)\bigr).\]
Consequently, requiring \(a(x)^\top u+b(x)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) is unchanged when \(U\) is replaced by its convex hull or closed convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For constraints affine in uncertainty, replacing an uncertainty set by its convex hull or closed convex hull leaves the robust constraint unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Invariance Principle

assumptions_latex: Uncertainty components may vary independently across the Cartesian factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{U_1\times\cdots\times U_k}(y_1,\ldots,y_k)=\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_{U_i}(y_i)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent block uncertainty and its separable support function.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Data uncertainty in Linear Optimization p. 27

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty sets \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_i}\), independent block uncertainty is represented by
\[U=U_1\times\cdots\times U_k=\{(u_1,\ldots,u_k):u_i\in U_i\text{ for every }i\}.\]
For every conformal direction \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_k)\), its support function separates as
\[\sigma_U(y)=\sup_{u_i\in U_i}\sum_{i=1}^k y_i^\top u_i=\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_{U_i}(y_i),\]
with equality understood in the extended-real sense. Thus separable affine robust terms decompose across the uncertainty blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent uncertainty blocks form a Cartesian product, and the support function of that product is the sum of the component support functions.
knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian-Product Uncertainty

children.title: Intersected Uncertainty Sets
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty geometries formed through intersections.

assumptions_latex: All component sets share the same uncertainty coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(U=\bigcap_{i=1}^kU_i\) is equivalent to simultaneous membership in every \(U_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection represented by stacking component constraints.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Data uncertainty in Linear Optimization p. 27

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The intersection of uncertainty sets \(U_1,\ldots,U_k\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is
\[U=\bigcap_{i=1}^kU_i=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:u\in U_i\text{ for every }i\}.\]
If each component has a lifted conic representation
\[U_i=\{u:\exists z_i,\ A_i u+B_i z_i+b_i\in K_i\},\]
then the intersection is represented by imposing all component systems simultaneously, using separate auxiliary variables \(z_i\). If every \(U_i\) is convex, then \(U\) is convex; closedness is likewise preserved by finite intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersected uncertainty requires every component description simultaneously; finite intersections preserve convexity and closedness of closed component sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Intersected Uncertainty Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty uncertainty set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), a linear map \(A:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^p\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), define
\[V=AU+b=\{Au+b:u\in U\}.\]
For every \(y\in\mathbb R^p\),
\[\sigma_V(y)=\sup_{u\in U}y^\top(Au+b)=b^\top y+\sigma_U(A^\top y).\]
Thus a robust linear maximization over the image is evaluated by pulling the direction back through \(A^\top\). Linear images preserve convexity but do not generally preserve closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of an affine image equals the offset term plus the original support function evaluated at the transposed direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Image Uncertainty
