children.title: Support Calculus for Intersections
children.top_down_role: Support-function structure associated with intersected sets.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_k\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) are nonempty closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_C\) is the lower-semicontinuous hull of the infimal convolution of \(\sigma_{C_1},\ldots,\sigma_{C_k}\).

notation.meaning: Lower-semicontinuous hull in the direction variable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closed-convex support calculus with closure made explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty closed convex sets with nonempty intersection \(C=\bigcap_{i=1}^kC_i\). Then
\[\sigma_C(y)=\operatorname{cl}\!\left(\inf_{y_1+\cdots+y_k=y}\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_{C_i}(y_i)\right),\qquad y\in\mathbb R^m,\]
where \(\operatorname{cl}\) denotes the lower-semicontinuous hull as a function of \(y\). Under the qualification \(\bigcap_{i=1}^k\operatorname{ri}C_i\ne\varnothing\), the closure may be omitted and the infimum is attained whenever its value is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of an intersection is the closed infimal convolution of the component support functions; relative-interior regularity yields an exact attained formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Calculus for Intersections

children.title: Preimage Representation Routes
children.top_down_role: Preimage-based descriptions for linearly transformed uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Preimage Representation Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted representation of uncertainty sets formed by intersections of affine preimages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_j\subseteq\mathbb R^{m_j}\), let \(T_j:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^{m_j}\) be linear, and let \(t_j\in\mathbb R^{m_j}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\). Define \(U=\bigcap_{j=1}^rT_j^{-1}(V_j-t_j)=\{u:T_ju+t_j\in V_j\ \forall j\}\). Then the robust constraint \(g(x,u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in U\) is equivalently imposed over lifted variables by requiring \(g(x,u)\leq0\) for every \((u,v_1,\ldots,v_r)\) satisfying \(v_j=T_ju+t_j\) and \(v_j\in V_j\) for all \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intersection of affine preimages admits an exact lifted description, so robust feasibility may be checked over linked uncertainty variables in their original sets.
assumptions_latex: \(g:X\times\mathbb R^q\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is defined on the represented uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall u\in U,\ g(x,u)\leq0\iff\forall (u,v):[v_j=T_ju+t_j,\ v_j\in V_j\ \forall j]\Rightarrow g(x,u)\leq0\).

notation.meaning: Affine preimage of the set V_j under u mapped to T_j u+t_j.

knowledge_statements.title: Semi-Infinite Constraint View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise-indexed representation of a robust scalar constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(U\) be a nonempty uncertainty set, and let \(f:X\times U\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). The robust feasible set generated by one uncertain scalar constraint is \(F=\{x\in X:f(x,u)\leq0\ \text{for every }u\in U\}\). Thus one robust constraint is exactly the semi-infinite family \(f(x,u)\leq0\), indexed by \(u\in U\). When \(U\) is infinite, this family may contain infinitely many constraints despite having finitely many decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust scalar constraint is exactly a family of deterministic constraints indexed by every uncertainty realization.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x,u)\) is defined for every \((x,u)\in X\times U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F\iff f(x,u)\leq0\quad\forall u\in U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Feasibility View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case adversarial interpretation of robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty uncertainty set \(U\) and constraint function \(f:X\times U\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), define the adversarial value \(v(x)=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\). A decision \(x\in X\) is robustly feasible exactly when \(v(x)\leq0\). If \(v(x)>0\), then either some \(u\in U\) satisfies \(f(x,u)>0\), or there exists a sequence \((u_k)\subseteq U\) with \(f(x,u_k)\to v(x)>0\); hence the adversary supplies an actual or asymptotic violation witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust feasibility means that an adversary choosing the uncertainty cannot make the constraint value positive.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x,u)\) is defined as an extended-real value on \(X\times U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x,u)\leq0\ \forall u\in U\iff \sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\leq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Supremum Value Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case value function associated with an uncertainty-indexed constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a convex subset of a real vector space, let \(U\neq\varnothing\), and let \(f:X\times U\to\overline{\mathbb R}\). The supremum value function is \(v:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) defined by \(v(x)=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\). Its zero sublevel set is precisely the robust feasible set. If \(f(\cdot,u)\) is convex on \(X\) for every \(u\in U\), then \(v\) is convex because it is a pointwise supremum of convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The supremum value function records the worst constraint value; its zero sublevel set is robustly feasible, and it preserves pointwise convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f(\cdot,u)\) is convex for every \(u\in U\) when the convexity conclusion is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(x)=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u),\qquad \{x:v(x)\leq0\}=\{x:f(x,u)\leq0\ \forall u\in U\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact support-function form for constraints affine in uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be nonempty, and consider \(a(x)+\langle b(x),u\rangle\leq0\) for every \(u\in U\). With the extended-real support function \(\sigma_U(y)=\sup_{u\in U}\langle y,u\rangle\), the worst-case left-hand side equals \(a(x)+\sigma_U(b(x))\). Consequently, the uncertain family has the exact deterministic counterpart \(a(x)+\sigma_U(b(x))\leq0\), including the convention that an infinite support value makes the constraint infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine uncertain constraint reduces exactly to one inequality involving the uncertainty set's support function.
assumptions_latex: \(a:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) and \(b:X\to\mathbb R^q\) are defined at the decision considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+\langle b(x),u\rangle\leq0\ \forall u\in U\iff a(x)+\sigma_U(b(x))\leq0\).

notation.meaning: Support function of U at y.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Based Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust counterpart for a positive-radius gauge-sublevel uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be closed and convex with \(0\) in its interior, and let \(C^\circ=\{y:\langle y,c\rangle\leq1\ \forall c\in C\}\). For \(\rho>0\), the gauge ball \(U_\rho=\{u:\gamma_C(u)\leq\rho\}\) equals \(\rho C\), and \(\sigma_{U_\rho}(y)=\rho\gamma_{C^\circ}(y)\). Hence the robust affine constraint over \(U_\rho\) is exactly \(a(x)+\rho\gamma_{C^\circ}(b(x))\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive radius, uncertainty bounded by a gauge yields a robust penalty equal to the radius times the polar gauge.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is closed and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+\langle b(x),u\rangle\leq0\ \forall u:\gamma_C(u)\leq\rho\iff a(x)+\rho\gamma_{C^\circ}(b(x))\leq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Set Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust counterpart when uncertainty is a scaled polar set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be closed and convex with \(0\) in its interior, and set \(U=\rho C^\circ\) for \(\rho\geq0\). The support function of this uncertainty set satisfies \(\sigma_U(y)=\rho\sigma_{C^\circ}(y)=\rho\gamma_C(y)\). Therefore the family \(a(x)+\langle b(x),u\rangle\leq0\) for all \(u\in U\) is equivalent to the polar-set counterpart \(a(x)+\rho\gamma_C(b(x))\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For uncertainty in a scaled polar set, the worst-case affine penalty is the corresponding primal gauge.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is closed and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+\langle b(x),u\rangle\leq0\ \forall u\in\rho C^\circ\iff a(x)+\rho\gamma_C(b(x))\leq0\).

notation.meaning: Polar of the reference set C.

children.title: Gauge–Polar Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Representation correspondence between gauge functionals and polar sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge–Polar Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real gauge and support identities under polarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) containing \(0\), define \(C^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\leq1\ \forall x\in C\}\). Then, as extended-real functions, \(\gamma_C(x)=\sigma_{C^\circ}(x)\) and \(\sigma_C(y)=\gamma_{C^\circ}(y)\). Thus a gauge description of uncertainty and a support-function description over its polar are interchangeable; if \(C\) is unbounded or not absorbing, the identities remain valid with possible infinite values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge of a closed convex set equals the support function of its polar, and conversely.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C=\sigma_{C^\circ},\qquad \sigma_C=\gamma_{C^\circ}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extended-real gauge-polar identities are correct for a nonempty closed convex set containing the origin, but no source is supplied.

children.title: Nonclosed Polarity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Closure-sensitive limits of gauge-polar counterpart representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Polarity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information lost when polarity is applied to nonclosed or nonconvex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^q\), polarity satisfies \(S^\circ=(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S\cup\{0\}))^\circ\) and the bipolar identity gives \(S^{\circ\circ}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S\cup\{0\})\). Consequently, polar-based reconstruction does not recover a nonclosed or nonconvex uncertainty set itself; it recovers its closed convex hull after adjoining the origin. Exact identities such as \(S^{\circ\circ}=S\) therefore require \(S\) to be closed, convex, and to contain \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity forgets nonclosure and nonconvexity: bipolar reconstruction returns the closed convex hull with the origin adjoined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^{\circ\circ}=S\iff S\text{ is closed, convex, and }0\in S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polarity and bipolar statements correctly describe the closed-convex-origin hull recovered from an arbitrary set, and failure_boundary is the appropriate content kind. No source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Duality Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact LP-dual reformulation for polyhedral uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^q:Du\leq d\}\) be nonempty and consider \(a(x)+b(x)^\top u\leq0\) for every \(u\in U\). If \(\sup_{u\in U}b(x)^\top u\) is finite, linear-programming strong duality yields \(\sup_{Du\leq d}b(x)^\top u=\min\{d^\top\lambda:D^\top\lambda=b(x),\ \lambda\geq0\}\). Hence robust feasibility is equivalent to the existence of \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying \(D^\top\lambda=b(x)\) and \(a(x)+d^\top\lambda\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral uncertainty can be eliminated exactly using nonnegative linear-programming dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+b(x)^\top u\leq0\ \forall u\in U\iff\exists\lambda\geq0:\ D^\top\lambda=b(x),\ a(x)+d^\top\lambda\leq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Duality Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic-dual elimination of affine uncertainty under Slater regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^q:d-Du\in K\}\). Suppose there exists \(\bar u\) with \(d-D\bar u\in\operatorname{int}K\), and the support problem has finite value. Conic strong duality gives \(\sup_{u\in U}b(x)^\top u=\min\{d^\top\lambda:D^\top\lambda=b(x),\ \lambda\in K^*\}\). Therefore the robust affine constraint is equivalent to the existence of such a dual multiplier satisfying \(a(x)+d^\top\lambda\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under conic Slater regularity, a robust affine constraint becomes finite constraints involving a dual-cone multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+b(x)^\top u\leq0\ \forall u\in U\iff\exists\lambda\in K^*:\ D^\top\lambda=b(x),\ a(x)+d^\top\lambda\leq0\).

children.title: Fenchel-Dual Counterparts
children.top_down_role: Counterpart representations based on convex conjugacy.

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Dual Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate representation for additively penalized uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb R^q\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and define its Fenchel conjugate by \(\phi^*(y)=\sup_{u\in\mathbb R^q}\{\langle y,u\rangle-\phi(u)\}\). The uncertainty-penalized family \(a(x)+\langle b(x),u\rangle-\phi(u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in\operatorname{dom}\phi\) is equivalent to \(a(x)+\phi^*(b(x))\leq0\). Thus Fenchel conjugation eliminates the universal uncertainty quantifier exactly, with extended-real values representing unbounded worst-case exposure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel conjugation converts a universally quantified affine-minus-convex penalty into one deterministic conjugate inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:\mathbb R^q\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(a(x)\) and \(b(x)\) are defined at the decision considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(x)+\langle b(x),u\rangle-\phi(u)\leq0\ \forall u\in\operatorname{dom}\phi\iff a(x)+\phi^*(b(x))\leq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantified inequality is exactly equivalent to the conjugate inequality and duality is an appropriate content kind, but the record supplies no source or locator.

children.title: Lagrangian-Dual Counterparts
children.top_down_role: Counterpart representations based on multiplier dualization.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian-Dual Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar robust constraints over convex inequality descriptions of the uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^q:g_j(u)\le 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), where every \(g_j\) is proper convex, and let \(u\mapsto f(x,u)\) be concave and upper semicontinuous for fixed \(x\). Define \(p(x)=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\) and \(L_x(u,\lambda)=f(x,u)-\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jg_j(u)\). Weak duality gives \(p(x)\le d(x):=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\sup_u L_x(u,\lambda)\). Hence the existence of \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(\sup_uL_x(u,\lambda)\le0\) is a safe robust counterpart. If strong duality holds and the dual infimum is attained, this condition is equivalent to \(f(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lagrange multipliers yield a safe finite certificate for a robust constraint; strong duality and dual attainment make the certificate exact.
assumptions_latex: \(U\neq\varnothing\) and the displayed suprema are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists\lambda\ge0:\ \sup_u L_x(u,\lambda)\le0\ \Longrightarrow\ \sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\le0,\] with equivalence under strong duality and dual attainment.

notation.meaning: Worst-case value of the uncertain constraint.

children.title: Conjugate–Multiplier Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate–Multiplier Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perspective-conjugate form of a single convex uncertainty-set multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex, let \(U=\{u:g(u)\le0\}\), and suppose a Slater point \(\bar u\) satisfies \(g(\bar u)<0\). For \(z\in\mathbb R^q\), Lagrangian duality and conjugacy give \[\sigma_U(z)=\sup_{g(u)\le0}\langle z,u\rangle=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}(\lambda g)^*(z).\] For \(\lambda>0\), \((\lambda g)^*(z)=\lambda g^*(z/\lambda)\); at \(\lambda=0\), the term is interpreted as the closed perspective value. Thus the multiplier formulation and the perspective of the Fenchel conjugate are the same robust-counterpart representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative uncertainty-set multiplier becomes the perspective variable of the Fenchel conjugate, giving an exact support-function formula under Slater regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sigma_U(z)=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}(\lambda g)^*(z)=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\operatorname{clpersp}(g^*)(z,\lambda).\]

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the uncertainty-set function.
Support function of the uncertainty set.

children.title: Duality-Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where dual counterpart representations lose exactness.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for dual certificates of scalar robust constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(\Lambda\neq\varnothing\), and let \(p:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) and \(D:X\times\Lambda\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) satisfy \(p(x)\le D(x,\lambda)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(\lambda\in\Lambda\). Define \(d(x)=\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda}D(x,\lambda)\). Then every certificate \(D(x,\lambda)\le0\) is safe. For a robust-feasible point \(x\), a certificate necessarily exists when \(d(x)<0\); when \(d(x)=0\), it exists exactly when the infimum is attained; and when \(d(x)>0\), no certificate exists. Hence a positive duality gap causes conservative rejection only when \(p(x)\le0<d(x)\), while zero gap without attainment obstructs certification only at the boundary \(p(x)=d(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual certificates are always safe. A negative dual value is certifiable even without attainment, whereas a zero dual value requires attainment; conservative rejection occurs when a robust-feasible point has positive dual value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{x\in X:\exists\lambda\in\Lambda,\ D(x,\lambda)\le0\}=\{x\in X:p(x)\le0\}\] if and only if every \(x\) with \(p(x)\le0\) satisfies either \(d(x)<0\), or \(d(x)=0\) with the infimum attained.

notation.meaning: Infimum of the dual certificate values.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Wise Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of a robust constraint system into scalar row counterparts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i:X\times U_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). The robust system \(F_i(x,u_i)\le0\) for every \(u_i\in U_i\) and every row \(i\) is equivalent to the conjunction of scalar worst-case inequalities \[\sup_{u_i\in U_i}F_i(x,u_i)\le0,\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.\] The equivalence also holds when all rows share one uncertainty vector and one set \(U\), because the universal quantifier distributes over a finite conjunction. Row-wise reformulation does not require the worst cases of different rows to occur at the same uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite robust system equals the conjunction of its scalar row worst-case constraints, even when different rows attain different worst cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall i\ \forall u_i\in U_i:\ F_i(x,u_i)\le0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \forall i:\ \sup_{u_i\in U_i}F_i(x,u_i)\le0.\]

notation.meaning: Uncertain scalar function in row i.
Uncertainty set relevant to row i.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Block Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cartesian uncertainty blocks with an additively separable uncertain function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(K\in\mathbb N\), and let \(U=U_1\times\cdots\times U_K\) with every \(U_k\neq\varnothing\). Let \(a:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) and \(F_k:X\times U_k\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and define \(F(x,u)=a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K F_k(x,u_k)\) for \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_K)\). Whenever these extended-real sums are well-defined, \[\sup_{u\in U}F(x,u)=a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K\sup_{u_k\in U_k}F_k(x,u_k).\] Consequently, the robust constraint is equivalent to the existence of \(t\in\mathbb R^K\) satisfying \(F_k(x,u_k)\le t_k\) for every \(u_k\in U_k\) and every \(k\), together with \(a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K t_k\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many nonempty Cartesian uncertainty blocks and an additively separable uncertain function, the worst-case value is the sum of the block worst-case values, and finite epigraph bounds give an exact coupled representation.
assumptions_latex: All displayed extended-real sums are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup_{u\in U}F(x,u)\le0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists t\in\mathbb R^K:\ \sup_{u_k\in U_k}F_k(x,u_k)\le t_k\ \forall k,\quad a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K t_k\le0.\]

notation.meaning: Term depending only on uncertainty block k.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph variables separate sums of worst-case component values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_k:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be worst-case component functions, for example \(h_k(x)=\sup_{u_k\in U_k}F_k(x,u_k)\), and let \(a:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Whenever the sum is well-defined, \[a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K h_k(x)\le0\] is equivalent to the existence of \(t\in\mathbb R^K\) such that \(h_k(x)\le t_k\) for every \(k\) and \(a(x)+\sum_k t_k\le0\). Thus each component epigraph may be reformulated independently and coupled only by the final scalar inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary epigraph bounds separate component worst-case terms while a single scalar inequality preserves their total robust constraint exactly.
assumptions_latex: The displayed extended-real sum is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[a(x)+\sum_k h_k(x)\le0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists t\in\mathbb R^K:\ h_k(x)\le t_k\ \forall k,\ a(x)+\sum_k t_k\le0.\]

children.title: Lifted-Variable Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition organized through extended-variable representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Variable Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact replacement of component epigraphs by projected lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(K\in\mathbb N\), let \(a:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and let \(h_k:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,K\). For each \(k\), let \(Y_k\) and \(Z_k\) be sets, let \(K_k\subseteq Z_k\), and let \(G_k:X\times\mathbb R\times Y_k\to Z_k\) satisfy \[\operatorname{epi}h_k=\{(x,t_k)\in X\times\mathbb R:\exists y_k\in Y_k,\ G_k(x,t_k,y_k)\in K_k\}.\] Whenever \(a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K h_k(x)\) is well-defined, the constraint \(a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K h_k(x)\le0\) is equivalent to the existence of \(t\in\mathbb R^K\) and \(y_k\in Y_k\) satisfying \(G_k(x,t_k,y_k)\in K_k\) for every \(k\) and \(a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K t_k\le0\). Equality in every lifted epigraph representation is required for exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact lifted epigraph representations introduce block-local witnesses and preserve the aggregate constraint after projection; a one-sided outer representation need not be exact.
assumptions_latex: For every \(k\), the displayed lifted projection equals \(\operatorname{epi}h_k\).
The aggregate extended-real sum is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K h_k(x)\le0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists t\in\mathbb R^K\ \exists y_k\in Y_k\ (k=1,\ldots,K):\ G_k(x,t_k,y_k)\in K_k\ \forall k,\quad a(x)+\sum_{k=1}^K t_k\le0.\]

notation.meaning: Block-local lifted variable belonging to Y_k.
Lifted constraint mapping for block k.

children.title: Extended-Formulation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coupling introduced by auxiliary variables across decomposed components.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Formulation Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier-compatible coupling condition for exact extended robust formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let block relations be \(C_k\subseteq X\times Y_0\times Y_k\), where \(x\) is the original decision, \(y_0\) is a shared lift, and \(y_k\) is block-local. The extended formulation represents \[S=\{x:\exists y_0\ \exists y_1,\ldots,y_K,\ (x,y_0,y_k)\in C_k\ \text{for all }k\}.\] Decomposition may eliminate each \(y_k\) separately because all local existential quantifiers occur inside the same shared choice of \(y_0\). It is generally invalid to replace the common-lift condition by independently chosen \(y_{0k}\), since \(\forall k\,\exists y_{0k}\) does not imply \(\exists y_0\,\forall k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block lifts may be separated only while preserving shared auxiliary variables and quantifier order; independently chosen copies can enlarge the projected feasible set.
assumptions_latex: Each block relation uses the same original variable \(x\) and shared lift \(y_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in S\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists y_0:\ \bigwedge_{k=1}^K\bigl(\exists y_k:\ (x,y_0,y_k)\in C_k\bigr).\]

notation.meaning: Auxiliary variable local to block k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantifier-order condition is plausible and appropriately classified, but the record has no citation or marked standard-field rationale supporting the nontrivial claim about independently copied shared lifts.

children.title: Projection Recovery Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for recovering original-space counterpart descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Recovery Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of original robust decisions from an exact lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq X\times Y\) be a lifted robust-counterpart feasible set and let \(S\subseteq X\) be the intended feasible set in the original variables. The lift is exact at the recovery interface if and only if \[S=\operatorname{proj}_X E=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in E\}.\] Every lifted feasible point then recovers a feasible original decision by discarding \(y\), and every \(x\in S\) admits at least one lifted witness. If only \(\operatorname{proj}_X E\subseteq S\) holds, the formulation is safe but potentially conservative; the reverse inclusion alone is an unsafe relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection exactly recovers robust decisions when lifted feasibility and original feasibility have witnesses in both directions; one-sided inclusions characterize conservative or unsafe formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S=\operatorname{proj}_X E\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl((x,y)\in E\Rightarrow x\in S\bigr)\ \text{and}\ \bigl(x\in S\Rightarrow\exists y:(x,y)\in E\bigr).\]

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the lifted counterpart.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection characterization is standard and fits the property leaf, but no evidence is supplied. The displayed conclusion should also bind its variables universally when the record is sourced.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Attainment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case attainment for continuous uncertain constraints on compact uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be any decision set, let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be nonempty and compact, and let \(f:X\times U\to\mathbb R\) be such that \(f(x,\cdot)\) is upper semicontinuous for every fixed \(x\). Then, for each \(x\in X\), there exists \(u_x\in U\) with \[\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)=f(x,u_x)=\max_{u\in U}f(x,u).\] Consequently, \(f(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) if and only if \(f(x,u_x)\le0\) for every maximizer \(u_x\). Compactness removes nonattainment of the primal worst case, though it does not by itself guarantee attainment of a dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper-semicontinuous uncertainty dependence over a nonempty compact set attains its worst case, eliminating primal nonattainment but not necessarily dual nonattainment.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x,\cdot)\) is upper semicontinuous for each \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in X\ \exists u_x\in U:\ \sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)=f(x,u_x).\]

notation.meaning: A worst-case uncertainty realization for decision x.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Duality Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slater regime for exact Lagrangian robust counterparts with dual attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\), and consider \(p(x)=\sup\{f(x,u):g_j(u)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), where \(f(x,\cdot)\) is proper concave upper semicontinuous and each \(g_j\) is proper closed convex. Assume the value is finite and there exists \(\bar u\in\operatorname{ri}(\bigcap_j\operatorname{dom}g_j)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f(x,\cdot))\) satisfying \(g_j(\bar u)<0\) for every \(j\). Then \[p(x)=\min_{\lambda\ge0}\sup_u\left(f(x,u)-\sum_j\lambda_jg_j(u)\right).\] Therefore the Lagrangian robust counterpart is exact and possesses a finite multiplier certificate whenever \(p(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior Slater point yields zero duality gap and multiplier attainment, making the Lagrangian robust counterpart exact.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x,\cdot)\) is proper concave upper semicontinuous and \(p(x)\) is finite.
The displayed relative-interior strict-feasibility condition holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p(x)\le0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists\lambda\ge0:\ \sup_u\left(f(x,u)-\sum_j\lambda_jg_j(u)\right)\le0.\]

children.title: Closure-Sensitive Counterparts
children.top_down_role: Counterpart representations affected by closure operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Sensitive Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact recovery when closure is interchanged with lifted projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closed convex lifted feasible set can have a nonclosed projection. For example, define \[E=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\ge 1/x\}.\] The set \(E\) is closed and convex, while \(\operatorname{proj}_xE=(0,\infty)\) and \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{proj}_xE)=[0,\infty)\). Thus replacing an existential lifted counterpart by the closure of its projection admits \(x=0\), although no finite witness \(y\) exists there. Closure is harmless only when the relevant projection is known to be closed or when the intended original feasible set is itself the closed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing a nonclosed projected counterpart can add boundary decisions with no finite lifted certificate, so closure and existential projection are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: Only finite lifted witnesses \(y\in\mathbb R\) are admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{proj}_xE=(0,\infty)\subsetneq[0,\infty)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{proj}_xE).\]

notation.meaning: Closed convex lifted feasible set in the example.
Projection onto the original scalar variable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example is mathematically consistent: the displayed epigraph is closed and convex, its projection is open, and closure adds a point without a finite witness. Nevertheless, the record supplies no source or marked standard-field rationale for this nontrivial failure-boundary claim.

children.title: Nonattained Worst Cases
children.top_down_role: Worst-case values lacking realizing uncertainty scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonattained Worst Cases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of worst-scenario attainment for continuous uncertain constraints over nonclosed uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be nonempty and let \(g(x,u)\) be continuous in \(u\). Robust feasibility is characterized by \(\sup_{u\in U}g(x,u)\le 0\), whether or not the supremum is attained. Consequently, replacing the supremum by a maximum or demanding a worst-case scenario can be invalid when \(U\) is not compact. For example, with \(U=(0,1)\) and \(g(x,u)=u-x\), robust feasibility is exactly \(x\ge 1\). At \(x=1\), every scenario satisfies \(g(1,u)<0\), but \(\sup_{u\in U}g(1,u)=0\) and no \(u\in U\) attains this value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust supremum may determine feasibility without being attained; over an open interval, every scenario can be slack while the limiting worst-case value is zero.
assumptions_latex: For each fixed \(x\), the map \(u\mapsto g(x,u)\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in U}g(x,u)\le 0\) need not admit any maximizing \(u\in U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary example and supremum claim fit the terminal container and are mathematically plausible, but no citation is supplied. The ambient space for U and the domain of x and g should also be specified when authoritative support is added.

children.title: Limiting Certificate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Certificates available only through limiting objects or sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Limiting Certificate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential certificates for an unattained finite worst-case value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)=\sup_{u\in U}g(x,u)<+\infty\). A limiting worst-case certificate is a sequence \((u_k)_{k\ge1}\subset U\) satisfying \(g(x,u_k)\to v(x)\). Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), some \(u_\varepsilon\in U\) satisfies \(g(x,u_\varepsilon)>v(x)-\varepsilon\). If \(v(x)=0\) and the supremum is not attained, these scenarios certify arbitrarily small robust slack, although no single scenario certifies equality. If \(v(x)>0\), sufficiently advanced members of the sequence are explicit violating scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no worst scenario exists, a maximizing sequence certifies the limiting margin and eventually exposes infeasibility whenever the supremum is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x,u_k)\to v(x)\) supplies an asymptotically exact certificate of the worst-case value.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximizing-sequence statement is an appropriate certificate for this terminal container, but it has no cited source. The domains of x, U, and g also remain implicit.

children.title: Open-Set Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Attainment failures associated with nonclosed uncertainty regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Open-Set Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary behavior of continuous robust constraints over open uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be nonempty and let \(g(x,\cdot)\) extend continuously to \(\operatorname{cl}U\). Then \(g(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) if and only if \(g(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in\operatorname{cl}U\). However, pointwise strict feasibility on \(U\) does not imply a uniform negative margin. Indeed, for \(U=(0,1)\) and \(g(x,u)=u-x\), the point \(x=1\) satisfies \(g(1,u)<0\) for every \(u\in U\), while \(\sup_{u\in U}g(1,u)=0\). Thus strict scenario inequalities can converge to an active excluded boundary scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous nonstrict robust constraints extend to the closure, but strict inequalities on an open set need not provide any uniform robust slack.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise strictness on \(U\) does not imply \(\sup_{u\in U}g(x,u)<0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closure and strict-margin claims match the failure-boundary container, but no source is cited. A sourced version should identify the ambient topological space in which closure and continuity are taken.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertain Linear Rows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rowwise robust interpretation of an uncertain linear inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each row \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let the coefficient pair \((a_i(u),b_i(u))\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\) depend on \(u\in U_i\). The uncertain linear row is \(a_i(u)^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i(u)\). Its robust counterpart requires the same decision \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) to satisfy every realization: \[a_i(u)^{\mathsf T}x-b_i(u)\le0\quad\text{for all }u\in U_i,\quad i=1,\ldots,m.\] Equivalently, each row obeys \(\sup_{u\in U_i}\{a_i(u)^{\mathsf T}x-b_i(u)\}\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncertain linear system is robustly feasible when one decision satisfies every realization of every uncertain row.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is chosen before uncertainty is revealed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is robustly feasible exactly when \(\sup_{u\in U_i}(a_i(u)^{\mathsf T}x-b_i(u))\le0\) for every \(i\).

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Uncertain Linear Problems and their Robust Counterparts p. 32

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertain Linear Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust counterpart when uncertainty occurs only in a scalar right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) be fixed and let the bound be \(b(u)\in\mathbb R\) for \(u\in U\). The uncertain inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u)\) is required for every realization. Its exact robust counterpart is \[a^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{u\in U}b(u).\] This equality of feasible sets remains valid when the infimum is not attained. If \(\inf_{u\in U}b(u)=-\infty\), no finite \(x\) can satisfy the robust row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right-hand-side uncertainty replaces the uncertain bound by its infimum, even when no scenario attains that infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u)\ \forall u\in U\iff a^{\mathsf T}x\le\inf_{u\in U}b(u)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertain Linear-Objective Epigraphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph reformulation of a worst-case uncertain linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(U\neq\varnothing\), and let \(c(u)\in\mathbb R^n\). The robust objective \(\min_{x\in X}\sup_{u\in U}c(u)^{\mathsf T}x\) has the exact epigraph formulation \[\min_{x,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\in X,\qquad c(u)^{\mathsf T}x\le t\quad\text{for all }u\in U.\] For every fixed \(x\), the least admissible epigraph value is \(t=\sup_{u\in U}c(u)^{\mathsf T}x\), provided this supremum is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst-case linear objective becomes an epigraph variable constrained above every realized objective value.
assumptions_latex: The decision \(x\) is selected before \(u\) is revealed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge c(u)^{\mathsf T}x\ \forall u\in U\iff t\ge\sup_{u\in U}c(u)^{\mathsf T}x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Linear Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite counterpart for a linear row with finitely many scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the uncertainty set consist of scenarios \(U=\{u^1,\ldots,u^K\}\). For an uncertain linear row \(a(u)^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u)\), the robust requirement is exactly the finite linear system \[a(u^k)^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u^k),\qquad k=1,\ldots,K.\] Thus each uncertain row produces one deterministic linear inequality per scenario. No convexification of \(U\) changes the counterpart when \(a(u)\) and \(b(u)\) depend affinely on \(u\), because an affine residual attains its supremum over the scenario convex hull at a scenario extreme point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite uncertainty is handled exactly by imposing one deterministic linear inequality for each scenario and each uncertain row.
assumptions_latex: The uncertain constraint is linear in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(u)^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u)\ \forall u\in U\iff a(u^k)^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u^k)\ \forall k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the uncertain residual be \(\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}z\), where \(z\in U=\{z\in\mathbb R^p:|z_j|\le\rho_j\}\) and \(\rho_j\ge0\). Then \[\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}z\le0\quad\text{for all }z\in U\] is equivalent to \[\alpha(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\rho_j|q_j(x)|\le0.\] If \(\alpha\) and every \(q_j\) are affine, an exact linear formulation introduces \(s_j\ge q_j(x)\), \(s_j\ge-q_j(x)\), and imposes \(\alpha(x)+\sum_j\rho_js_j\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Box uncertainty adds the weighted absolute values of uncertain-direction coefficients to the nominal row residual.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{z\in\mathbb R^p:Dz\le d\}\) be nonempty and let the uncertain residual be \(\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}z\). The robust inequality \(\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}z\le0\) for all \(z\in U\) holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[D^{\mathsf T}\lambda=q(x),\qquad \alpha(x)+d^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le0.\] This is the linear-programming dual of the support-function problem \(\sup\{q(x)^{\mathsf T}z:Dz\le d\}\). If \(\alpha\) and \(q\) are affine, the counterpart is a linear system in \((x,\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual multipliers replace a polyhedral worst-case maximization, yielding an exact deterministic linear system.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^p\), let \(\|\cdot\|_*\) be its dual norm, and let \(U=\{z:\|z\|\le\rho\}\) with \(\rho\ge0\). For the affine-in-uncertainty residual \(\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}z\), the robust inequality over \(U\) is equivalent to \[\alpha(x)+\rho\|q(x)\|_*\le0.\] Indeed, the worst-case uncertainty contribution is the support function \(\sup_{\|z\|\le\rho}q(x)^{\mathsf T}z=\rho\|q(x)\|_*\). The deterministic counterpart is convex whenever \(\alpha\) and \(q\) are affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm-ball uncertainty set contributes its radius times the dual norm of the uncertain-direction vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal-Uncertainty Conic-Quadratic Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order-cone counterpart for an ellipsoidal uncertain linear row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{\bar z+P w:w\in\mathbb R^r,\ \|w\|_2\le1\}\). For the uncertain linear residual \(\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}z\), robust feasibility is equivalent to \[\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}\bar z+\|P^{\mathsf T}q(x)\|_2\le0.\] If \(\alpha\) and \(q\) are affine, this is represented by an auxiliary variable \(t\) satisfying \(\|P^{\mathsf T}q(x)\|_2\le t\) and \(\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}\bar z+t\le0\), hence it is a conic-quadratic counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ellipsoidal uncertainty yields a second-order-cone term equal to the Euclidean norm of the transformed uncertain-direction vector.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha\) and \(q\) are affine when conic representability is claimed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{z\in U}(\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}z)=\alpha(x)+q(x)^{\mathsf T}\bar z+\|P^{\mathsf T}q(x)\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Gamma-Robust Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear counterpart for budgeted independent coefficient deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\sum_{j=1}^n(\bar a_j+d_jz_j)x_j\le b\), where \(d_j\ge0\) and \(Z_\Gamma=\{z:|z_j|\le1,\ \sum_j|z_j|\le\Gamma\}\). Its exact robust counterpart is the existence of \(s,p\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(\pi\ge0\) such that \[s_j\ge x_j,\quad s_j\ge-x_j,\quad \pi+p_j\ge d_js_j\quad(j=1,\ldots,n),\] \[\sum_{j=1}^n\bar a_jx_j+\Gamma\pi+\sum_{j=1}^np_j\le b.\] The parameter \(0\le\Gamma\le n\) limits the aggregate simultaneous deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gamma robustness protects against a budgeted collection of coefficient deviations and has an exact linear extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed linear system is equivalent to \(\sum_j(\bar a_j+d_jz_j)x_j\le b\) for every \(z\in Z_\Gamma\).

notation.meaning: maximum deviation magnitude of coefficient j
dual variables for the deviation-budget problem

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For row \(i\), define the protection function by \[\beta_i(x,\Gamma_i)=\max\left\{\sum_{j=1}^n d_{ij}|x_j|z_j:0\le z_j\le1,\ \sum_{j=1}^n z_j\le\Gamma_i\right\}.\] If the uncertain coefficient is \(a_{ij}=a_{ij}^0+d_{ij}\xi_{ij}\), with \(|\xi_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sum_j|\xi_{ij}|\le\Gamma_i\), then \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\) for every admissible \(\xi_i\) if and only if \((a_i^0)^\top x+\beta_i(x,\Gamma_i)\le b_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The protection function is the largest budget-admissible coefficient deviation. Adding it to the nominal row gives an exact robust counterpart.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Parameter Linear Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static robust linear systems whose rows are parameterized by one common uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A shared-parameter robust linear system is the family \[a_i(u)^\top x\le b_i(u),\qquad i=1,\ldots,m,\quad u\in U,\] interpreted as \(\forall u\in U\), \(\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). The same realization \(u\) determines all row data in a joint evaluation. Its robust feasible set is \[\left\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i(u)^\top x\le b_i(u)\text{ for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\text{ and every }u\in U\right\}.\] Replacing the common parameter by independently selected row parameters changes the joint uncertainty model, even though for this static universally quantified system the feasible set can be computed rowwise using the corresponding row projections of \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All rows are parameterized by one common uncertainty realization. This specifies their joint uncertainty model, although static robust feasibility can still be tested row by row using projected uncertainty sets.
assumptions_latex: \(n,m,p\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty.
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(a_i:U\to\mathbb R^n\) and \(b_i:U\to\mathbb R\) are affine maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i(u)^\top x\le b_i(u)\) holds for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and every common \(u\in U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Joint-Budget Linear Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted coefficient uncertainty whose joint uncertainty set has one aggregate budget across all rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A joint-budget linear uncertainty set is \[\mathcal Z_\Gamma=\left\{z\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:0\le z_{ij}\le1,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n z_{ij}\le\Gamma\right\}.\] With \(a_{ij}=a_{ij}^0+s_{ij}d_{ij}z_{ij}\), where \(s_{ij}\in[-1,1]\), the robust system requires \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\) for every coefficient array generated by one \(z\in\mathcal Z_\Gamma\) and one admissible sign array \(s\). The aggregate bound couples the joint uncertainty set across rows. For this static universally quantified system, however, robust feasibility is equivalent to protecting each row against its projected budget set, because all deviations outside that row may be set to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One aggregate budget defines the joint coefficient uncertainty set across all rows. In a static universally robust system, its feasible set nevertheless equals the intersection of the rowwise robust sets obtained from the corresponding projections.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and the rows are indexed by \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint uncertainty allocation satisfies \(\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n z_{ij}\le\Gamma\).

knowledge_statements.title: Globally Coupled Linear Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global robust feasibility represented by the worst row violation under a common uncertainty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define \[G(x)=\sup_{u\in U}\max_{1\le i\le m}\left\{a_i(u)^\top x-b_i(u)\right\}.\] Then the uncertain linear system \(a_i(u)^\top x\le b_i(u)\) for every \(i\in\{1,,m\}\) and every common \(u\in U\) is equivalent to \(G(x)\le0\). Moreover, because the row index set is finite, \[G(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\sup_{u\in U}\left(a_i(u)^\top x-b_i(u)\right).\] Thus the scalar global-violation representation preserves the shared parameterization, while static robust feasibility may equivalently be checked rowwise over the row projections of \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global robust feasibility is equivalent to requiring the worst row violation over all common uncertainty realizations to be nonpositive; for finitely many rows, the same feasibility test can be evaluated rowwise.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n,p\in\mathbb N\), \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty, and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(u\in U\), \(g_i(x,u)=a_i(u)^\top x-b_i(u)\), where \(a_i(u)\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b_i(u)\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is robustly feasible if and only if \(\sup_{u\in U}\max_{1\le i\le m}g_i(x,u)\le0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) by \(F(x)=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\). For \(x,y\in X\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\), \[F(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\le\theta F(x)+(1-\theta)F(y).\] Hence \(F\) is convex on \(X\). In particular, the robust constraint \(f(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\), equivalently \(F(x)\le0\), has a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst-case supremum of functions convex in the decision is convex, so its robust zero-sublevel set is convex.

Thus the robust worst-case problem admits a saddle-point characterization.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Uncertain Conic-Quadratic Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-scenario expansion of an uncertain second-order-cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and consider \(\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2\le c(u)^\top x+d(u)\) for every \(u\in U\). If \(U=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\), define \((A_k,b_k,c_k,d_k)=(A(u^k),b(u^k),c(u^k),d(u^k))\). Its robust counterpart is exactly \[\|A_kx+b_k\|_2\le c_k^\top x+d_k,\qquad k=1,\ldots,N.\] Hence finite scenario uncertainty produces a finite second-order-cone system without relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many uncertainty scenarios, robust conic-quadratic feasibility is exactly one second-order-cone constraint per scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(n,q,N\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(U=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\) is a finite nonempty scenario set.
For every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(b_k\in\mathbb R^q\), \(c_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d_k\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust constraint is exactly \(\|A_kx+b_k\|_2\le c_k^\top x+d_k\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Uncertain Conic-Quadratic Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box uncertainty in affine conic-quadratic data; no generic vertex-reduction claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interval-uncertain conic-quadratic constraint is \[\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2\le c(u)^\top x+d(u)\qquad\text{for every }u\in U,\] where \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(U=\prod_{j=1}^p[\underline u_j,\overline u_j]\), and the data maps are affine in \(u\). Equivalently, defining \[F(x)=\sup_{u\in U}\left(\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2-c(u)^\top x-d(u)\right),\] robust feasibility is \(F(x)\le0\). This definition alone does not imply that checking only the vertices of \(U\) is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval uncertainty requires a conic-quadratic inequality for every point in a parameter box; vertex checking is not generically asserted.
assumptions_latex: \(n,p,q\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(U=\prod_{j=1}^p[\underline u_j,\overline u_j]\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is a nonempty box.
The affine maps satisfy \(A(u)\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(b(u)\in\mathbb R^q\), \(c(u)\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d(u)\in\mathbb R\) for every \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust feasibility is equivalent to \(\sup_{u\in U}(\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2-c(u)^\top x-d(u))\le0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Bounded Conic-Quadratic Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine data uncertainty over a prescribed norm ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:\|u\|\le\rho\}\). For affine data maps, the robust conic-quadratic constraint \[\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2\le c(u)^\top x+d(u)\qquad\text{for every }u\in U\] is equivalent to \[\sup_{\|u\|\le\rho}\left(\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2-c(u)^\top x-d(u)\right)\le0.\] For every fixed \(u\), the residual is convex in \(x\); consequently, its supremum is convex independently of whether a finite conic reformulation is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm-bounded robust conic-quadratic feasibility is the nonpositivity of the worst residual over a norm ball, and that residual supremum is convex in the decision.
assumptions_latex: \(n,p,q\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\rho\ge0\), and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:\|u\|\le\rho\}\), where \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on \(\mathbb R^p\).
The affine maps satisfy \(A(u)\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(b(u)\in\mathbb R^q\), \(c(u)\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d(u)\in\mathbb R\) for every \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust constraint is \(\sup_{\|u\|\le\rho}(\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2-c(u)^\top x-d(u))\le0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal Conic-Quadratic Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-image Euclidean-ball uncertainty; semidefinite representability is not claimed generically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(U=\{\bar u+Qv:v\in\mathbb R^r,\ \|v\|_2\le1\}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\). The ellipsoidally uncertain conic-quadratic constraint \(\|A(u)x+b(u)\|_2\le c(u)^\top x+d(u)\) for every \(u\in U\) is equivalent to \[\sup_{\|v\|_2\le1}\left(\|A(\bar u+Qv)x+b(\bar u+Qv)\|_2-c(\bar u+Qv)^\top x-d(\bar u+Qv)\right)\le0.\] Exact semidefinite or conic reformulations require additional structural hypotheses on how the uncertain data enter the constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ellipsoidal uncertainty is an affine image of a Euclidean ball; robust feasibility controls the worst conic-quadratic residual over that ball.
assumptions_latex: \(n,p,q,r\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^p\), \(Q\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}\), and \(U=\{\bar u+Qv:v\in\mathbb R^r,\ \|v\|_2\le1\}\).
The affine maps satisfy \(A(u)\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(b(u)\in\mathbb R^q\), \(c(u)\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d(u)\in\mathbb R\) for every \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust feasibility is equivalent to the stated worst-case inequality over \(\{v\in\mathbb R^r:\|v\|_2\le1\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unstructured Norm-Bounded Quadratic Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact robust counterpart for one quadratic inequality over a Euclidean norm ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(u)=u^{\mathsf T}Qu+2a^{\mathsf T}u+r\), where \(Q\in\mathbb S^m\), and let \(\rho>0\). Then \(q(u)\le 0\) for every \(u\) satisfying \(\lVert u\rVert_2\le\rho\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[\begin{pmatrix}Q-\lambda I&a\\a^{\mathsf T}&r+\lambda\rho^2\end{pmatrix}\preceq0.\] Thus an unstructured norm-bounded robust quadratic constraint has an exact semidefinite representation with one nonnegative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic inequality holds throughout a Euclidean ball exactly when a single S-lemma multiplier makes the associated block matrix negative semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho>0\), so the uncertainty ball has nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(u)\le0\ \forall u:\lVert u\rVert_2\le\rho\iff\exists\lambda\ge0:\begin{pmatrix}Q-\lambda I&a\\a^{\mathsf T}&r+\lambda\rho^2\end{pmatrix}\preceq0\).

notation.meaning: Radius of the Euclidean uncertainty ball.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Ellipsoid Quadratic Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact S-lemma representation for uncertainty confined to one full-dimensional ellipsoid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(u)=u^{\mathsf T}Qu+2a^{\mathsf T}u+r\), let \(W\succ0\), and define \(\mathcal U=\{u:(u-\bar u)^{\mathsf T}W(u-\bar u)\le1\}\). Put \(c=\bar u^{\mathsf T}Q\bar u+2a^{\mathsf T}\bar u+r\). Then \(q(u)\le0\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\) if and only if some \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfies \[\begin{pmatrix}Q-\lambda W&Q\bar u+a\\(Q\bar u+a)^{\mathsf T}&c+\lambda\end{pmatrix}\preceq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robustness over one full-dimensional ellipsoid is exactly characterized by a negative-semidefinite block matrix with one nonnegative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(u)\le0\ \forall u\in\mathcal U\iff\exists\lambda\ge0:\begin{pmatrix}Q-\lambda W&Q\bar u+a\\(Q\bar u+a)^{\mathsf T}&c+\lambda\end{pmatrix}\preceq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Quadratic Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine shared-parameter structure in the coefficients of a robust quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) and let \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\). A structured quadratically uncertain constraint is \[x^{\mathsf T}\!\left(A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m u_iA_i\right)x+2\left(b_0+\sum_{i=1}^m u_ib_i\right)^{\mathsf T}x+c_0+\sum_{i=1}^m u_ic_i\le0\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U.\] The same parameter vector \(u\) jointly controls prescribed coefficient directions, distinguishing structured uncertainty from independent perturbation of all coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured quadratic uncertainty uses one shared parameter vector to vary prescribed matrix, linear, and constant coefficient directions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is the prescribed uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is robustly feasible exactly when the displayed quadratic inequality holds for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection-of-Ellipsoids Quadratic Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-ellipsoid S-procedure certificate, sufficient but generally not exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\ge1\), \(q(u)=u^{\mathsf T}Qu+2a^{\mathsf T}u+r\), and \(\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:u^{\mathsf T}W_ju\le1,\ j=1,\ldots,k\}\), where \(W_j\succ0\). If there exist \(\lambda_j\ge0\) such that \[\begin{pmatrix}Q-\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_jW_j&a\\a^{\mathsf T}&r+\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j\end{pmatrix}\preceq0,\] then \(q(u)\le0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\). For \(k>1\), failure to find these scalar multipliers does not generally imply failure of the robust inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers yield a verifiable semidefinite certificate over an intersection of centered ellipsoids, but the certificate can be conservative when several ellipsoids are present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k\ge0\) satisfying the displayed matrix inequality implies \(q(u)\le0\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unstructured Norm-Bounded Matrix Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict robust matrix inequality under one full, real, spectral-norm-bounded block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\in\mathbb S^n\), \(L\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(R\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\). The strict robust matrix inequality \[F+L\Delta R+R^{\mathsf T}\Delta^{\mathsf T}L^{\mathsf T}\prec0\quad\forall\Delta\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}:\lVert\Delta\rVert_2\le1\] holds if and only if there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfying \[F+\varepsilon LL^{\mathsf T}+\varepsilon^{-1}R^{\mathsf T}R\prec0.\] This is the exact scalar-multiplier reduction for a single unstructured norm-bounded real matrix block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict matrix inequality robust to one full spectral-norm-bounded block is equivalent to a deterministic inequality with one positive scaling parameter.

\(\Delta\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) is otherwise unstructured and satisfies \(\lVert\Delta\rVert_2\le1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact LMI robust counterpart for unstructured norm-bounded quadratic uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representation of the robust counterpart of constraints (7.13)–(7.14); the underlying constraints and Theorem 7.2 remain required context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(L(y)=[L_A(y),L_b(y),L_c(y)]\), \(\widehat L^T(y)=[L_b^T(y)+\tfrac12L_c^T(y);L_A^T(y)]\), \(\widehat R(y)=[R(y),0_{q\times k}]\), and \(\mathcal A(y)=\begin{bmatrix}2y^Tb^{\mathrm n}+c^{\mathrm n}&(A^{\mathrm n}y)^T\\A^{\mathrm n}y&I_k\end{bmatrix}\). Assume these matrices are affine in \(y\) and at least one of \(\widehat L(y),\widehat R(y)\) is constant. If \(\widehat L\) is constant and nonzero, the robust counterpart is equivalent to the existence of \(\lambda\) such that \(\begin{bmatrix}\mathcal A(y)-\lambda\widehat L^T\widehat L&\widehat R^T(y)\\\widehat R(y)&\lambda I_q\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\). If \(\widehat R\) is constant and nonzero, it is equivalently represented by the existence of \(\lambda\) such that \(\begin{bmatrix}\mathcal A(y)-\lambda\widehat R^T\widehat R&\widehat L^T(y)\\\widehat L(y)&\lambda I_p\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\). If \(\widehat L\equiv0\) or \(\widehat R\equiv0\), it reduces to \(\mathcal A(y)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the robust counterpart of constraints (7.13)–(7.14), a nonzero constant L-hat or R-hat factor yields the corresponding exact block-LMI representation with an auxiliary scalar lambda. If either factor is identically zero, the robust constraint reduces to positive semidefiniteness of A(y). When both factors are constant and nonzero, either applicable block-LMI representation is valid.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{RC}\text{ is the robust counterpart of (7.13) and (7.14)}
\mathcal A(y),\widehat L(y),\widehat R(y)\text{ are affine in }y
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\widehat L\text{ constant},\ \widehat L\ne0\implies\left[\operatorname{RC}\iff\exists\lambda:\begin{bmatrix}\mathcal A(y)-\lambda\widehat L^T\widehat L&\widehat R^T(y)\\\widehat R(y)&\lambda I_q\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right],\\&\widehat R\text{ constant},\ \widehat R\ne0\implies\left[\operatorname{RC}\iff\exists\lambda:\begin{bmatrix}\mathcal A(y)-\lambda\widehat R^T\widehat R&\widehat L^T(y)\\\widehat L(y)&\lambda I_p\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\right],\\&(\widehat L\equiv0\ \lor\ \widehat R\equiv0)\implies\left[\operatorname{RC}\iff\mathcal A(y)\succeq0\right].\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe LMI approximation for structured norm-bounded uncertain LMIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the auxiliary LMI system, its safety guarantee, rank-dependent tightness bound, and its exactness cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A_\zeta(y)\succeq0\) have structured norm-bounded uncertainty of level \(\rho\). Suppose variables \(y\), \(Y_\ell\), and \(\lambda_\ell\) satisfy \[Y_\ell\succeq \pm\mathcal A_\ell(y)\quad(\ell\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm s}),\] \[\begin{bmatrix}\lambda_\ell I_{p_\ell}&L_\ell(y)\\L_\ell(y)^T&Y_\ell-\lambda_\ell R_\ell^TR_\ell\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\quad(\ell\notin\mathcal I_{\mathrm s}),\] and \[\mathcal A^{\mathrm n}(y)-\rho\sum_{\ell=1}^L Y_\ell\succeq0.\] Then \(\mathcal A_\zeta(y)\succeq0\) for every \(\zeta\in\mathcal Z_\rho\). The approximation has tightness factor at most \(\vartheta(\mu)\), where \(\mu\) is the smallest integer at least \(2\) such that \(\mu\geq\max_y\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal A_\ell(y))\) for every \(\ell\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm s}\), with \(\vartheta(2)=\pi/2\), \(\vartheta(4)=2\), and \(\vartheta(\mu)\leq\pi\sqrt{\mu/2}\) for \(\mu>2\). The approximation is exact if \(L=1\), or if all perturbations are scalar and every \(\mathcal A_\ell(y)\) has rank at most \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a structured norm-bounded uncertain LMI, feasibility of the auxiliary LMIs guarantees positive semidefiniteness for every admissible perturbation. The approximation has a universal rank-dependent tightness bound and is exact for one uncertainty block or for scalar perturbations with rank-at-most-one coefficient matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_\zeta(y)\) has the structured norm-bounded form with uncertainty set \(\mathcal Z_\rho\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A_\zeta(y)\succeq0\) for every \(\zeta\in\mathcal Z_\rho\), with tightness factor at most \(\vartheta(\mu)\) and exactness if \(L=1\), or if all perturbations are scalar and the coefficient matrices have rank at most one.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Matrix-Inequality Control Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LMI interface from norm-bounded robust stability to state-feedback synthesis variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), \(E\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), and consider \(\dot x=(A+BK+H\Delta E)x\) with \(K\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(\Delta\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) satisfying \(\lVert\Delta\rVert_2\le1\). If there exist \(X\in\mathbb S^n_{++}\), \(Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{He}(AX+BY)+\varepsilon HH^{\mathsf T}&XE^{\mathsf T}\\EX&-\varepsilon I_q\end{pmatrix}\prec0,\] then \(K=YX^{-1}\) robustly stabilizes every admissible system. The matrix \(P=X^{-1}\) is the associated common quadratic Lyapunov certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block LMI in explicitly dimensioned transformed variables certifies a state-feedback gain and a common quadratic Lyapunov matrix for every norm-bounded plant perturbation.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstructured Robust Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact regularized form for a full norm-bounded perturbation of the augmented data matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=[A\ -b]\), \(z=(x^{\mathsf T},1)^{\mathsf T}\), and let an unstructured perturbation satisfy \(\lVert\Delta\rVert_2\le\rho\). Then \[\max_{\lVert\Delta\rVert_2\le\rho}\lVert(M+\Delta)z\rVert_2=\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2+\rho\sqrt{\lVert x\rVert_2^2+1}.\] Consequently, minimizing the worst-case least-squares residual is equivalent to minimizing the convex regularized expression on the right. Its epigraph is second-order-cone representable by separately bounding the two displayed norms and their weighted sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full norm-bounded perturbations turn least squares exactly into residual norm plus a norm penalty on the augmented decision vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_x\max_{\lVert\Delta\rVert_2\le\rho}\lVert(M+\Delta)z\rVert_2=\min_x\bigl(\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2+\rho\sqrt{\lVert x\rVert_2^2+1}\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Robust Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact S-lemma epigraph for affine residual uncertainty over one Euclidean ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the residual be \(r(u,x)=r_0(x)+R(x)u\), with \(u\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\lVert u\rVert_2\le1\). For fixed \(x\) and \(t\ge0\), the robust bound \(\lVert r(u,x)\rVert_2\le t\) for every admissible \(u\) holds if and only if some \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfies \[\begin{pmatrix}R(x)^{\mathsf T}R(x)-\lambda I&R(x)^{\mathsf T}r_0(x)\\r_0(x)^{\mathsf T}R(x)&\lVert r_0(x)\rVert_2^2-t^2+\lambda\end{pmatrix}\preceq0.\] This captures correlated coefficient perturbations through the shared vector \(u\).

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Linear Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax linear estimator for bounded combined signal and noise energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(y=Cx+Dw\), the target is \(z=Lx\), and the estimate is \(\widehat z=Ky\). For \(\xi=(x^{\mathsf T},w^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) satisfying \(\lVert\xi\rVert_2\le1\), the worst-case estimation error is \[\max_{\lVert\xi\rVert_2\le1}\lVert z-\widehat z\rVert_2=\lVert[\,L-KC\ \ -KD\,]\rVert_2.\] Therefore an optimal robust linear estimator minimizes \(t\) subject to \[\begin{pmatrix}tI&L-KC&-KD\\(L-KC)^{\mathsf T}&tI&0\\-D^{\mathsf T}K^{\mathsf T}&0&tI\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\] with identity-block dimensions chosen compatibly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case error of a linear estimator over an energy ball equals an induced matrix norm, yielding a semidefinite minimax design.
assumptions_latex: \(y=Cx+Dw\), \(z=Lx\), and \(\widehat z=Ky\) have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_K\max_{\lVert\xi\rVert_2\le1}\lVert z-Ky\rVert_2\) equals the optimum of the displayed semidefinite program in \((K,t)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Form Support Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard uncertainty sets whose support functions admit explicit finite formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty compact convex set \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), define \(\sigma_{\mathcal U}(z)=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}z^{\mathsf T}u\). For \(\rho\ge0\), any norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^d\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{d\times s}\), \(\ell,h\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\ell\le h\), and vertices \(v^1,\ldots,v^N\in\mathbb R^d\), closed forms include \[\sigma_{\{u\in\mathbb R^d:\lVert u\rVert\le\rho\}}(z)=\rho\lVert z\rVert_*,\qquad \sigma_{\bar u+P\mathbb B_2^s}(z)=z^{\mathsf T}\bar u+\lVert P^{\mathsf T}z\rVert_2,\] \[\sigma_{[\ell,h]}(z)=\sum_{i=1}^d\max\{\ell_i z_i,h_i z_i\},\qquad \sigma_{\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}}(z)=\max_{1\le j\le N}z^{\mathsf T}v^j.\] These formulas convert robust affine inequalities into explicit norm, separable, or finite-maximum constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm balls, affine images of Euclidean balls, boxes, and vertex-listed polytopes have explicit support functions that directly produce robust affine counterparts.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_*\) is dual to the norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) on \(\mathbb R^d\).
\(\mathbb B_2^s=\{v\in\mathbb R^s:\lVert v\rVert_2\le1\}\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{d\times s}\), and \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed uncertainty families admit the stated closed-form support functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Representable Support Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional lifted conic uncertainty sets under strong conic duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a closed convex cone, \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times k}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^k,\ Au+Bz+b\in K\}\). If this conic system is strictly feasible and \(\sigma_U(c)<+\infty\) for \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), then conic strong duality gives \[\sigma_U(c)=\min_{y\in K^*}\{b^\top y:A^\top y=-c,\ B^\top y=0\}.\] Consequently, for \(t\in\mathbb R\), the inequality \(\sigma_U(c)\le t\) is equivalent to the existence of \(y\in K^*\) satisfying \(A^\top y=-c\), \(B^\top y=0\), and \(b^\top y\le t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict feasibility and finite support, a lifted conic uncertainty set yields an exact support constraint represented by a dual-cone variable and affine equations.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is a closed convex cone with dual cone \(K^*\).
There exist \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar z\in\mathbb R^k\) such that \(A\bar u+B\bar z+b\in\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_U(c)\le t\) has an exact finite-dimensional conic representation over \(K^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G=(V,E)\), let \(U=\operatorname{STAB}(G)\). For every nonnegative weight vector \(c\in\mathbb Q^{V}_+\), \[\sigma_U(c)=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in S}c_i:S\subseteq V\text{ is stable}\right\}.\] Thus support evaluation contains maximum-weight stable set and is NP-hard. Deciding the robust inequality \(c^\top u\le t\) for every \(u\in U\) is equivalent to deciding \(\sigma_U(c)\le t\), so an exact robust counterpart cannot generally be obtained in polynomial time from an arbitrary compact uncertainty-set description unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support evaluation can encode maximum-weight stable set; therefore exact robust enforcement is generally intractable for compact combinatorial uncertainty descriptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a closed convex cone and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^k,\ Au+Bz+b\in K\}\). knowledge_statements.title: Nonexact Dualization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between safe weak-duality reformulations and exact strong-duality counterparts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^k,\ Au+Bz+b\in K\}\), define \(p^*=\sup_{u\in U}c^\top u\) and \[d^*=\inf\{b^\top y:y\in K^*,\ A^\top y=-c,\ B^\top y=0\}.\] Weak duality gives \(p^*\le d^*\). Consequently, any \(y\in K^*\) satisfying \(A^\top y=-c\), \(B^\top y=0\), and \(b^\top y\le t\) certifies \(c^\top u\le t\) for every \(u\in U\). Without strong duality and dual attainment, one may have \(p^*<d^*\), or \(p^*=d^*\) with no dual minimizer. Thus replacing the robust inequality by existence of such a dual certificate can be conservative and need not be equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strong duality or dual attainment, correctly signed conic dual constraints remain safe certificates but may reject genuinely robust decisions.
assumptions_latex: A weak-duality certificate is formed for the conic support maximization problem associated with \(Au+Bz+b\in K\).
No constraint qualification guaranteeing strong duality or dual attainment is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual feasibility remains sufficient for robustness but need not be necessary.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(\|\cdot\|_*\) be its dual norm, and let \(U=\{\bar u+v:\|v\|\le\rho\}\), where \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\rho\ge0\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic representation of the dual-norm epigraph converts a robust linear constraint over a translated norm ball into an equivalent finite-dimensional conic system.

knowledge_statements.title: Lossless Single-Quadratic Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical real S-lemma with one strictly feasible quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), let \(q_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be given by \(q_i(u)=u^\top Q_i u+2a_i^\top u+r_i\), where \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_i\in\mathbb R\). If there exists \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(q_1(\bar u)<0\), then \[q_1(u)\le0\ \Longrightarrow\ q_0(u)\le0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R^n\] if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[q_0(u)-\lambda q_1(u)\le0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R^n.\] Thus the scalar S-procedure is lossless in the single-constraint Slater regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one strictly feasible quadratic constraint, the S-lemma makes a single nonnegative multiplier both sufficient and necessary for the quadratic implication.
assumptions_latex: \(q_0\) and \(q_1\) are real quadratic functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).
There exists \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(q_1(\bar u)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(q_1(u)\le0\Rightarrow q_0(u)\le0\) is equivalent to one nonnegative quadratic multiplier certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Quadratic Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite robust counterpart induced by the lossless single-constraint S-lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), let \(q_i(u)=u^\top Q_i u+2a_i^\top u+r_i\), where \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r_i\in\mathbb R\), and define \[M_i=\begin{bmatrix}Q_i&a_i\\a_i^\top&r_i\end{bmatrix}.\] Then \(q_i(u)=\begin{bmatrix}u\\1\end{bmatrix}^\top M_i\begin{bmatrix}u\\1\end{bmatrix}\). Under the strict-feasibility hypothesis \(q_1(\bar u)<0\) for some \(\bar u\in\mathbb R^n\), the implication \(q_1(u)\le0\Rightarrow q_0(u)\le0\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\) is equivalent to \[\exists\lambda\ge0:\quad M_0-\lambda M_1\preceq0.\] This linear matrix inequality is an exact semidefinite robust counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenizing the quadratics turns the lossless single-constraint S-lemma certificate into an exact linear matrix inequality.
assumptions_latex: The hypotheses of the single-constraint S-lemma hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Real Matrix-Cube Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real symmetric affine matrix uncertainty over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_0,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\). The real matrix-cube robust constraint is
\[
A(u):=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m u_iA_i\succeq0\quad\text{for every }u\in[-1,1]^m.
\]
Its feasible set, when the matrices also depend affinely on a decision vector \(x\in\mathbb R^p\), is \(F_{\mathbb R}:=\{x:A_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m u_iA_i(x)\succeq0\ \forall u\in[-1,1]^m\}\). All matrices and uncertainty coordinates are real.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real matrix-cube constraint requires a real symmetric affine matrix pencil to remain positive semidefinite for every real uncertainty vector in a box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in F_{\mathbb R}\iff A_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m u_iA_i(x)\succeq0\) for all \(u\in[-1,1]^m\).

knowledge_statements.title: Complex Matrix-Cube Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hermitian affine matrix uncertainty over complex unit discs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_0\in\mathbb H^n\) and \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\). The complex matrix-cube robust constraint is
\[
A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl(z_iB_i+\overline z_iB_i^*\bigr)\succeq0
\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb C^m\text{ with }|z_i|\le1.
\]
The paired terms make the uncertain matrix Hermitian. If the data depend affinely on \(x\), the complex robust feasible set consists of all decisions satisfying this universal inequality.
