knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Cube Approximation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex enumeration is exact but exponential for affine box uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a Hermitian affine pencil \(A(u)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^m u_iA_i\) with real \(u\in[-1,1]^m\), convexity of the positive-semidefinite cone gives
\[
A(u)\succeq0\ \forall u\in[-1,1]^m
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
A(v)\succeq0\ \forall v\in\{-1,1\}^m.
\]
Thus vertex testing is an exact finite representation, but it contains \(2^m\) matrix inequalities. Without additional structure, it does not yield a representation polynomial in the uncertainty dimension; polynomial-size conic constructions must therefore be treated as approximations or separately justified exact reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checking all box vertices exactly certifies an affine matrix cube, but requires exponentially many semidefinite constraints, marking the basic representation-size boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\) are Hermitian matrices of a common order.
The dependence on real uncertainty \(u\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact vertex enumeration uses \(2^m\) positive-semidefinite tests.

knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Class Escalation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robustification may require a stronger tractable conic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the nominal constraint be representable over a cone class \(\mathcal K_0\). Cone-class escalation occurs when an exact or certified-safe robust counterpart admits a polynomial-size formulation over a class \(\mathcal K_1\), but no formulation over \(\mathcal K_0\) is supplied or established. A standard hierarchy is
\[
\text{linear}\ \subseteq\ \text{second-order-conic}\ \subseteq\ \text{semidefinite-conic}.
\]
Escalation describes the representation used, not an unconditional impossibility result for weaker cones; absence of a weaker formulation alone does not prove that none exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robustification escalates cone class when its tractable reformulation uses a stronger cone family than the nominal model; this alone is not a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The nominal and robust formulations are finite-dimensional conic representations.
Polynomial size is measured in the encoded input length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A formulation over \(\mathcal K_1\supsetneq\mathcal K_0\) constitutes representation-level cone-class escalation.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust-Counterpart Hardness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates finite verification from polynomial-time robust optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a constraint function \(g(x,u)\), robust feasibility of a fixed decision asks whether
\[
\sup_{u\in U}g(x,u)\le0.
\]
If evaluating this supremum, or deciding whether it exceeds zero, is NP-hard for the admitted descriptions of \(g\) and \(U\), then a polynomial-time exact robust counterpart would imply a polynomial-time solution of that separation problem. Hence convexity in \(x\) alone does not guarantee tractability: hardness may enter through nonconvex uncertainty dependence, combinatorial uncertainty sets, or succinct descriptions having exponentially many relevant scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex decision model can still have an intractable robust counterpart when worst-case evaluation over uncertainty is computationally hard.
assumptions_latex: Robust feasibility is defined by the worst-case value over \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hard worst-case separation obstructs a polynomial-time exact robust counterpart unless the underlying complexity classes collapse.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe and tractable approximation of a robust conic constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines safety by projected feasible-set containment and tractability by efficient convex representation or computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the robust counterpart be \(A(\zeta)x+b(\zeta)=\alpha(x)\zeta+\beta(x)\in\mathbf Q\) for all \(\zeta\in\mathcal Z\), where \(A(\zeta)\) and \(b(\zeta)\) depend affinely on \(\zeta\). A system \(\mathcal S\) of convex constraints in \(x\) and optional auxiliary variables \(u\) is a safe approximation if \[\forall x,\quad \bigl[\exists u:(x,u)\text{ satisfies }\mathcal S\bigr]\Rightarrow\bigl[A(\zeta)x+b(\zeta)\in\mathbf Q\ \forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z\bigr].\] The approximation is tractable if \(\mathcal S\) is tractable, for example through an explicit conic-quadratic or semidefinite representation or efficiently computable constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe and Factor-Tight Tractable Approximation of a Robust SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines safety and uncertainty-radius tightness through projected feasible-set inclusions for the robust SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho>0\), let \(y=(x,t)\), and let \(\mathcal S_\rho\) be a finite system of explicitly computable convex constraints in \(y\), possibly with auxiliary variables \(u\). If \(\widehat Y_\rho\) is the projection of its solution set onto the \(y\)-space and \(Y_\rho\) is the feasible set of the robust counterpart, then \(\mathcal S_\rho\) is safe when \(\widehat Y_\rho\subseteq Y_\rho\). It is \(\vartheta\)-tight, for \(\vartheta\ge1\), when \[Y_\rho\supseteq\widehat Y_\rho\supseteq Y_{\vartheta\rho}.\] Equivalently, extendability of \(y\) to a feasible \((y,u)\) for \(\mathcal S_\rho\) implies robust feasibility at level \(\rho\), while nonextendability implies failure of robust feasibility at level \(\vartheta\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite convex lifted system is safe when every projected feasible point is robust feasible at the same uncertainty level. It is theta-tight when it also contains every point robust feasible at level theta rho; acceptance certifies feasibility at rho, while rejection certifies infeasibility at theta rho.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal S_\rho\text{ is a finite system of explicitly computable convex constraints}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal S_\rho\text{ is safe and }\vartheta\text{-tight}\iff Y_\rho\supseteq\widehat Y_\rho\supseteq Y_{\vartheta\rho}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tightness factor of a safe robust-approximation scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines multiplicative conservatism by nesting the projected approximation feasible set between robust feasible sets at two uncertainty radii.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\rho>0\), let \(X_\rho\) be the feasible set of \(\mathrm{RC}_\rho\), and let \(\widehat X_\rho=\operatorname{proj}_x(\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S_\rho))\), where \(\mathcal S_\rho\) is a finite, safe, tractable convex approximation of \(\mathrm{RC}_\rho\). The scheme has conservatism, or tightness factor, at most \(\vartheta\ge1\) if \[X_{\vartheta\rho}\subseteq\widehat X_\rho\subseteq X_\rho\qquad\forall\rho>0.\] Equivalently, extendability to a feasible point of \(\mathcal S_\rho\) implies membership in \(X_\rho\), while nonextendability implies nonmembership in \(X_{\vartheta\rho}\). If \(\vartheta=1\), then \(\widehat X_\rho=X_\rho\) for every \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safe approximation scheme has tightness factor at most theta when, for every positive uncertainty radius rho, its projected feasible set contains every point robustly feasible at radius theta times rho and contains only points robustly feasible at radius rho. A factor of one makes the approximation exact at every radius.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\rho>0,\quad X_{\vartheta\rho}\subseteq\widehat X_\rho\subseteq X_\rho;\qquad \vartheta=1\Rightarrow\widehat X_\rho=X_\rho\ \forall\rho>0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision domain, let \(U\) be an uncertainty set, and let \(g_j:X\times U\to\mathbb R\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\). Define \[F:=\{x\in X:g_j(x,u)\le0\ \forall u\in U,\ \forall j=1,\ldots,r\}.\] Let \(\widehat g_k:X\to\mathbb R\) for \(k=1,\ldots,q\) be tractably checkable and define \[F_{\mathrm{in}}:=\{x\in X:\widehat g_k(x)\le0\ \forall k=1,\ldots,q\}.\] The set \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\) is a safe inner approximation when \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq F\). A sufficient certificate is that, for every \(x\in X\), satisfaction of all inequalities \(\widehat g_k(x)\le0\) implies \(g_j(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) and every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tractable approximation is safe when its feasible set is contained in the exact robust feasible set; a pointwise implication from its tractable constraints to every robust constraint certifies that containment.
knowledge_statements.title: Safe Inner Approximations

knowledge_statements.title: Outer Value Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer feasible relaxations bound minimization values from below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimization of \(f(x)\) over an exact robust feasible set \(F\), and let \(F_{\mathrm{out}}\) be a tractable outer approximation satisfying \(F\subseteq F_{\mathrm{out}}\). Define
\[
v_{\mathrm{out}}:=\inf_{x\in F_{\mathrm{out}}}f(x),
\qquad
v_*:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x).
\]
Then \(v_{\mathrm{out}}\le v_*\). For maximization the inequality reverses. An optimizer of the outer problem need not be robustly feasible; the construction certifies an objective-value bound, not a feasible robust decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, optimizing over a tractable outer relaxation gives a lower bound on the exact robust value but may return an infeasible decision.
assumptions_latex: Both infima use the same extended-real objective \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{out}}\le v_*\) for minimization.

notation.meaning: Tractable outer approximation of the robust feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Paired Approximation-Quality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner and outer models bracket the exact robust optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization problem, suppose tractable sets satisfy \(F_{\mathrm{in}}\subseteq F\subseteq F_{\mathrm{out}}\). Let
\[
v_{\mathrm{out}}:=\inf_{x\in F_{\mathrm{out}}}f(x),
\quad v_*:=\inf_{x\in F}f(x),
\quad v_{\mathrm{in}}:=\inf_{x\in F_{\mathrm{in}}}f(x).
\]
Then \(v_{\mathrm{out}}\le v_*\le v_{\mathrm{in}}\). If finite values are attained, the computable gap \(v_{\mathrm{in}}-v_{\mathrm{out}}\) bounds the absolute suboptimality of an inner optimizer by the same quantity. The set inclusions and the two optimization results form a paired quality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tractable outer and safe inner models bracket the exact robust value; their value gap certifies the inner solution's worst-case absolute suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with a common objective \(f\).
The displayed values are finite when a finite gap is claimed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{out}}\le v_*\le v_{\mathrm{in}}\) and \(0\le v_{\mathrm{in}}-v_*\le v_{\mathrm{in}}-v_{\mathrm{out}}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\in\mathbb R^p\), set \(z=(1,u^T)^T\), and represent each quadratic by \(q_j(u)=\langle Q_j,zz^T\rangle\), where \(Q_j\in\mathbb S^{p+1}\) for \(j=0,1,\ldots,m\). For \(\mathcal U=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:q_j(u)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), the value \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}q_0(u)\) admits a rank-one lifting with \(Y=zz^T\). Dropping the constraint \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\) gives the semidefinite upper bound \[\widehat v=\sup\{\langle Q_0,Y\rangle:Y\succeq0,\ Y_{11}=1,\ \langle Q_j,Y\rangle\leq0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Therefore \(\widehat v\leq0\) is a sufficient condition for \(q_0(u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic uncertainty is lifted to a positive-semidefinite matrix, and removing the rank-one constraint produces an SDP upper bound that can certify robust feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform multiplicative quality measured as a function of uncertainty dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider nonnegative minimization instances whose uncertainty vectors lie in \(\mathbb R^d\). Let \(v(I)\) be the exact robust optimum and \(\widehat v(I)\) the optimum of a safe inner approximation, so \(v(I)\leq\widehat v(I)\). The approximation has dimension-dependent quality \(\alpha(d)\geq1\) on an instance class \(\mathfrak I_d\) when \[v(I)\leq\widehat v(I)\leq\alpha(d)v(I)\quad\text{for every }I\in\mathfrak I_d.\] The smallest admissible \(\alpha(d)\), with the convention that it is infinite if no finite bound exists, is the dimension-dependent approximation factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximation quality is dimension-dependent when a uniform objective-value factor depends only on the uncertainty dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(0<v(I)<\infty\) for instances used in the multiplicative ratio.
\(\widehat v(I)\) is produced by a safe inner approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(d)=\sup_{I\in\mathfrak I_d}\widehat v(I)/v(I)\) whenever all denominators are positive.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation factor indexed by geometric parameters of the uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma(\mathcal U)\) be a specified affine-invariant geometric parameter of a nonempty compact convex uncertainty set, such as an ellipsoidal distortion or symmetry coefficient. For nonnegative minimization instances, a safe approximation has geometry-dependent quality \(\alpha(\gamma)\geq1\) if \[v(I)\leq\widehat v(I)\leq\alpha(\gamma(\mathcal U_I))v(I)\] for every admissible instance \(I\). Thus instances of arbitrary ambient dimension share the same guarantee whenever their uncertainty sets have the same controlled geometry. The factor is meaningful only after the parameter \(\gamma\) and the normalized instance class are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximation factor may depend on a declared geometric parameter of the uncertainty set rather than solely on dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U_I\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ratio \(\widehat v(I)/v(I)\) is bounded by \(\alpha(\gamma(\mathcal U_I))\) uniformly over the normalized class.

notation.meaning: exact and approximate robust optimal values

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Exploiting Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quality guarantee controlled by declared sparsity, block, rank, or separability structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s(I)\) denote a structural complexity parameter of a robust instance, such as maximum interaction-block size, sparsity width, or perturbation rank. A safe approximation exploits this structure with factor \(\alpha(s)\) when, for every nonnegative minimization instance in the declared structured class, \[v(I)\leq\widehat v(I)\leq\alpha(s(I))v(I).\] If \(s(I)\) remains bounded along a sequence whose ambient dimensions grow, then the quality bound remains dimension-independent whenever \(\sup_{t\leq s(I)}\alpha(t)<\infty\). The parameter and structural decomposition must be computable from the input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structure-exploiting guarantee replaces ambient dimension by a smaller computable parameter such as block size, sparsity width, or rank.
assumptions_latex: \(s(I)\) is explicitly defined and computable from the instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded \(s(I)\) yields a uniform approximation ratio bounded by \(\alpha(s(I))\), independently of ambient dimension.

notation.meaning: exact and approximate robust optimal values

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Approximation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for absence of any finite uniform multiplicative approximation factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(I)>0\) and \(\widehat v(I)\geq v(I)\) be the exact and safely approximated optimal values of a minimization instance. The approximation gap is uncontrolled on a class \(\mathfrak I\) if \[\sup_{I\in\mathfrak I}\frac{\widehat v(I)}{v(I)}=+\infty.\] Equivalently, for every \(M>0\) there exists \(I_M\in\mathfrak I\) satisfying \(\widehat v(I_M)>Mv(I_M)\). This failure can persist despite feasibility safety: safety controls inclusion of feasible sets but, without normalized geometry or structural restrictions, supplies no uniform objective-quality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safe approximation has an uncontrolled gap when its objective ratio to the exact robust optimum is unbounded over the instance class.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat v(I)\geq v(I)\) arises from a safe inner approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite \(\alpha\) satisfies \(\widehat v(I)\leq\alpha v(I)\) for all \(I\in\mathfrak I\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unbounded-ratio criterion is mathematically coherent and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no citation. An authoritative locator is required before this nontrivial failure claim can enter candidate-review knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Trusted-Core Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested uncertainty region on which full robust protection is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be an ambient uncertainty set and let \(g:\mathbb R^m\to[0,+\infty]\) be a closed convex gauge or risk score. For a threshold \(\tau\geq0\), the trusted-core region is \[\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}=\{u\in\mathcal U:g(u)\leq\tau\}.\] A core-tail globalized robust model requires the original uncertain constraint \(f(x,u)\leq0\) without relaxation for every \(u\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\), while realizations outside this core may receive a prescribed nonnegative violation allowance. The core must be nonempty to define a protected nominal regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trusted core is a nonempty low-risk subset of uncertainty on which the original constraint must hold without permitted violation.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is closed and convex, and \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x,u)\leq0\) is imposed for every \(u\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\).

notation.meaning: gauge or risk score defining the core

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized-Tail Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer uncertainty region where constraint violation is bounded by a prescribed penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty closed trusted core \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\subseteq\mathcal U\), the tail region is \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm t}=\mathcal U\setminus\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\). Let \(p:\mathcal U\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfy \(p(u)=0\) on \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\), typically \(p(u)=\lambda\operatorname{dist}(u,\mathcal U_{\mathrm c})\) with \(\lambda\geq0\). A penalized-tail globalized constraint is \[f(x,u)\leq p(u)\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\] It enforces the unrelaxed constraint on the core and limits admissible violation in the tail according to distance or another declared severity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside the trusted core, constraint violation is allowed only up to a nonnegative penalty that vanishes on the core.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\) is nonempty and closed.
\(p\geq0\) on \(\mathcal U\) and \(p=0\) on \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x,u)\leq p(u)\) globally implies \(f(x,u)\leq0\) throughout \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm c}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Globalized Linear Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-conjugate counterpart for affine uncertainty with a convex violation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the uncertain linear inequality be \(a_0^Tx-b_0+u^T(A^Tx-d)\leq\pi(u)\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R^m\), where \(\pi\) is proper, closed, and convex. Taking the supremum over uncertainty gives \[a_0^Tx-b_0+\sup_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\{u^T(A^Tx-d)-\pi(u)\}\leq0.\] By the definition of the Fenchel conjugate, the globalized robust constraint is equivalently \[a_0^Tx-b_0+\pi^*(A^Tx-d)\leq0.\] Whenever the epigraph of \(\pi^*\) has a tractable conic representation, this equality yields a tractable deterministic counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine uncertain inequality with convex violation penalty reduces to a deterministic constraint containing the penalty’s Fenchel conjugate.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The globalized inequality is equivalent to \(a_0^Tx-b_0+\pi^*(A^Tx-d)\leq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalized Robust Counterpart of an Uncertain Linear Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines global robust feasibility with prescribed sensitivity through a semi-infinite family of relaxed uncertain linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\alpha\geq0\) and a perturbation structure \((\mathcal Z,\mathcal L,\|\cdot\|)\), a vector \(x\) is globally robust feasible with global sensitivity \(\alpha\) for the uncertain linear constraint precisely when
\[
\left(a^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell a^\ell\right)^Tx
\leq b^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell b^\ell
+\alpha\operatorname{dist}(\zeta,\mathcal Z\mid\mathcal L)
\quad\text{for every }\zeta\in\mathcal Z_+=\mathcal Z+\mathcal L.
\]
This semi-infinite constraint is called the globalized robust counterpart of the uncertain linear constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is globally robust feasible with sensitivity alpha when the uncertain linear inequality holds for every physically possible perturbation after allowing a relaxation equal to alpha times its cone-compatible distance from the normal perturbation range. This semi-infinite family is the globalized robust counterpart.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal Z,\mathcal L,\|\cdot\|)\text{ is a perturbation structure}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is globally robust feasible with sensitivity }\alpha\iff\left(a^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell a^\ell\right)^Tx\leq b^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\zeta_\ell b^\ell+\alpha\operatorname{dist}(\zeta,\mathcal Z\mid\mathcal L)\quad\forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z_+.

knowledge_statements.title: Globalized Conic Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalarized globalized counterpart for an affine uncertain conic inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a closed convex cone, let \(F(x,u)\) be affine in \(u\), and choose \(e\in\operatorname{int}K\). A globalized conic constraint permitting penalty \(\pi(u)\geq0\) is \[F(x,u)+\pi(u)e\in K\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathcal U.\] By dual-cone scalarization, this is equivalent to \[\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\{-\langle y,F(x,u)\rangle-\pi(u)\langle y,e\rangle\}\leq0\quad\text{for every }y\in K^*.\] Restricting to \(\langle y,e\rangle=1\) gives a normalized family whose inner supremum can be dualized when \(\mathcal U\) and \(\pi\) are conically representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalized uncertain conic inclusion is represented by worst-case scalar inequalities indexed by normalized elements of the dual cone.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone with \(e\in\operatorname{int}K\).
\(F(x,u)\) is affine in \(u\), and \(\pi\geq0\) on \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The globalized conic inclusion holds exactly when all displayed dual-cone scalar inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: interior cone direction used for violation allowance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-Structured Robust Feasibility with Global Sensitivities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines globalized robust feasibility when the perturbation is partitioned into blocks having separate sensitivity coefficients, norms, normal ranges, and directional cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \zeta=(\zeta^1,\ldots,\zeta^S), \mathcal Z=\mathcal Z^1\times\cdots\times\mathcal Z^S, \mathcal L=\mathcal L^1\times\cdots\times\mathcal L^S, and F_y(\zeta)=\left(P_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^d\zeta_\ell P_\ell\right)y-\left(p^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^d\zeta_\ell p^\ell\right). The candidate y is robust feasible with global sensitivities \alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_S if \operatorname{dist}(F_y(\zeta),\mathbf Q)\leq\sum_{s=1}^S\alpha_s\operatorname{dist}(\zeta^s,\mathcal Z^s\mid\mathcal L^s) for every \zeta\in\mathcal Z_+:=\mathcal Z+\mathcal L, where \operatorname{dist}(u,\mathbf Q)=\min_{v\in\mathbf Q}\|u-v\|_Q and \operatorname{dist}(\zeta^s,\mathcal Z^s\mid\mathcal L^s)=\min\{\|\zeta^s-v^s\|_s:v^s\in\mathcal Z^s,\ \zeta^s-v^s\in\mathcal L^s\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate is robust feasible with blockwise global sensitivities when its constraint violation over the product range enlarged by the product cone is bounded by the sum of the sensitivity-weighted directional distances of the perturbation blocks.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf Q\subseteq\mathbb R^k\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex, and }\|\cdot\|_Q\text{ is a norm on }\mathbb R^k
\mathcal Z^s\text{ is a nonempty, closed, convex normal perturbation range for each }s
\mathcal L^s\text{ is a closed convex cone for each }s
\|\cdot\|_s\text{ is a norm on perturbation block }s
y\text{ is a candidate for the affine uncertain constraint }F_y(\zeta)\in\mathbf Q
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z+\mathcal L,\quad \operatorname{dist}(F_y(\zeta),\mathbf Q)\leq\sum_{s=1}^S\alpha_s\operatorname{dist}(\zeta^s,\mathcal Z^s\mid\mathcal L^s)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semi-infinite feasibility characterization for a globalized robust conic counterpart
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes feasibility for the specified globalized robust counterpart through a robust conic inclusion and blockwise distance-to-recession-cone inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the uncertain conic constraint (12.4) and its globalized robust counterpart (12.6), a candidate \(y\) is feasible if and only if
\[
\left[P_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^d\zeta_\ell P_\ell\right]^Ty-\left[p^0+\sum_{\ell=1}^d\zeta_\ell p^\ell\right]\in Q
\quad\forall\zeta\in\mathcal Z=\mathcal Z^1\times\cdots\times\mathcal Z^S,
\]
and, for every \(s=1,\ldots,S\),
\[
\operatorname{dist}\!\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^d(P_\ell y-p^\ell)(E_s\zeta^s)_\ell,\operatorname{Rec}(Q)\right)\le\alpha_s
\quad\forall\zeta^s\in\mathcal L^s_{\|\cdot\|_s}:=\{z\in\mathcal L^s:\|z\|_s\le1\},
\]
where \(E_s\) is the natural embedding of \(\mathbb R^{d_s}\) into \(\mathbb R^d=\mathbb R^{d_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb R^{d_S}\), and
\[
\operatorname{dist}(u,\operatorname{Rec}(Q))=\min_{v\in\operatorname{Rec}(Q)}\|u-v\|_Q.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate y is feasible for the specified globalized robust conic counterpart exactly when the conic inclusion holds for every realization in the product uncertainty set and every uncertainty block satisfies its stated distance bound to the recession cone for all unit-norm directions in the corresponding subspace.
assumptions_latex: \text{The uncertain conic constraint (12.4) and its GRC (12.6) are fixed as in the proposition's context.}
E_s:\mathbb R^{d_s}\to\mathbb R^d\text{ is the natural embedding}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\text{ is feasible for the GRC (12.6)}\iff\text{the robust conic inclusion and every blockwise distance bound hold with the displayed universal quantifiers.}

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposable Globalized Counterparts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-separable worst-case representation for product uncertainty and additive penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_B)\in\mathcal U_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal U_B\), and suppose the globalized scalar constraint has separable form \[c(x)+\sum_{b=1}^B\phi_b(x,u_b)\leq\sum_{b=1}^B\pi_b(u_b)\quad\text{for every }u.\] Product uncertainty implies the exact decomposition \[\sup_u\sum_{b=1}^B\bigl(\phi_b(x,u_b)-\pi_b(u_b)\bigr)=\sum_{b=1}^B\sup_{u_b\in\mathcal U_b}\bigl(\phi_b(x,u_b)-\pi_b(u_b)\bigr).\] Consequently, introducing epigraph variables \(t_b\) yields the counterpart \(c(x)+\sum_bt_b\leq0\), with \(t_b\) bounding its corresponding block supremum. Each block may therefore be dualized independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product uncertainty and additive penalties separate one global worst-case constraint into independent blockwise suprema joined by a single coupling inequality.
assumptions_latex: The uncertain expression and penalty are additively separable by block.
Each block supremum is well-defined in \(\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The globalized counterpart is \(c(x)+\sum_bt_b\leq0\) with \(t_b\geq\sup_{u_b\in\mathcal U_b}(\phi_b(x,u_b)-\pi_b(u_b))\).

notation.meaning: epigraph bound for a block supremum

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(Z\) be a nonempty uncertainty set with \(U\subseteq Z\), let \(f:X\times Z\to\mathbb R\), let \(d(\cdot,U):Z\to[0,\infty)\), and let \(\rho\geq0\). Define \(\Psi:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) by \[\Psi(x)=\sup_{z\in Z}\{f(x,z)-\rho d(z,U)\}.\] If a tractable convex function \(\widehat\Psi:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfies \(\widehat\Psi(x)\geq\Psi(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \(\widehat\Psi(x)\leq0\) is a safe convex approximation of \(\Psi(x)\leq0\): every feasible \(x\) satisfies \(f(x,z)\leq\rho d(z,U)\) for all \(z\in Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any tractable convex upper bound on the worst penalized violation yields an inner approximation of the globalized robust feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe and Tractable Approximation of a Globalized Robust Counterpart
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines safety by projected feasible-set containment and tractability by efficient computability of the convex constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal S\) be a system of convex constraints in \(y\), \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_S)\ge 0\), and possibly auxiliary variables \(u\). It is a safe approximation of the given globalized robust counterpart \(\mathrm{GRC}\) if
\[
\forall (y,\alpha),\quad \bigl[\exists u:\ (y,\alpha,u)\in\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S)\bigr]\Rightarrow (y,\alpha)\in\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC}).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{proj}_{y,\alpha}\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S)\subseteq\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC}).
\]
The approximation is tractable when \(\mathcal S\) is tractable, for example when it is an explicit system of conic quadratic inequalities or linear matrix inequalities, or more generally when its constraints are efficiently computable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex lifted system safely approximates a given globalized robust counterpart when every feasible point projected from the lifted system is feasible for that counterpart. The approximation is tractable when the convex constraint system is efficiently computable, as with explicit conic quadratic inequalities or linear matrix inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal S\text{ is a convex constraint system in }(y,\alpha,u)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_{y,\alpha}\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S)\subseteq\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC})

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tightness Factor for a Safe Tractable GRC Approximation Scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a uniform multiplicative tightness guarantee for a parameterized family of safe tractable approximations of globalized robust counterparts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\{\mathcal S_\rho\}_{\rho>0}\) be an approximation scheme such that each \(\mathcal S_\rho\) is a finite system of efficiently computable convex constraints in \(y\), \(\alpha\ge 0\), and possibly auxiliary variables \(u\). For \(\vartheta\ge 1\), the scheme is a safe tractable approximation of the GRC, tight within factor \(\vartheta\), if for every \(\rho>0\) and every \((y,\alpha\ge0)\):
\[
\bigl[\exists u:\ (y,\alpha,u)\in\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S_\rho)\bigr]\Rightarrow (y,\alpha)\in\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC}_\rho),
\]
and
\[
\bigl[\nexists u:\ (y,\alpha,u)\in\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S_\rho)\bigr]\Rightarrow (y,\vartheta^{-1}\alpha)\notin\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC}_{\vartheta\rho}).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameterized approximation scheme is safe and tight within factor theta when each approximating system is safe for the counterpart at the same parameter, while failure to extend a point to that system guarantees that the point with alpha divided by theta is infeasible for the counterpart whose parameter is multiplied by theta.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal S_\rho\text{ is a finite system of efficiently computable convex constraints in }(y,\alpha,u)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\rho>0\ \forall(y,\alpha\ge0):\quad \operatorname{proj}_{y,\alpha}\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S_\rho)\subseteq\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC}_\rho),\quad (y,\alpha)\notin\operatorname{proj}_{y,\alpha}\operatorname{Feas}(\mathcal S_\rho)\Rightarrow(y,\vartheta^{-1}\alpha)\notin\operatorname{Feas}(\mathrm{GRC}_{\vartheta\rho})

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\Psi(x)=\sup_{z\in Z}\{f(x,z)-\rho d(z,U)\}\). Restricting the data to \(Z=U\) and \(\rho=0\) gives \(\Psi(x)=\sup_{z\in U}f(x,z)\), the ordinary robust residual. Consequently, for every data class in which deciding whether some \(x\in X\) satisfies \(f(x,z)\leq0\) for all \(z\in U\) is NP-hard, feasibility of the corresponding globalized counterpart is NP-hard as well. Globalization therefore cannot ensure tractability without additional structure on \(f\), \(U\), \(d\), or their representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globalized robust feasibility inherits NP-hardness from any ordinary robust subclass obtained by choosing zero penalty and identical ambient and core sets.
assumptions_latex: The globalized input class permits \(Z=U\) and \(\rho=0\).
The embedded ordinary robust feasibility problem is NP-hard under polynomial-size encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{ordinary robust feasibility}\leq_p\text{globalized-counterpart feasibility}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional embedding argument is coherent and failure_boundary is the correct role, but no source identifies an NP-hard ordinary robust subclass or its encoding assumptions. A specific hardness theorem or reduction locator is required before the complexity claim can be retained.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, let \(\xi:\Omega\to\Xi\) be a random element, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, and let \(F:X\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\) be measurable in its second argument. If a measurable set \(U_\epsilon\subseteq\Xi\) satisfies \(\mathbb P\{\xi\in U_\epsilon\}\geq1-\epsilon\), then \(F(x,u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in U_\epsilon\) implies \(\mathbb P\{F(x,\xi)\leq0\}\geq1-\epsilon\). If \(F(\cdot,u)\) is convex for every \(u\in U_\epsilon\), then \(\bigcap_{u\in U_\epsilon}\{x\in X:F(x,u)\leq0\}\) is convex. Thus any tractable robust counterpart over \(U_\epsilon\) is a safe convex inner approximation of the scalar chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enforcing a convex constraint on an uncertainty set carrying probability at least one minus epsilon safely enforces the chance constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, let \(\xi:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m\) be a random vector whose components may be dependent, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(a_0:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(a:X\to\mathbb R^m\). Dependence is retained through the joint function \(\Lambda_\xi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For dependent linear perturbations, the safe Bernstein counterpart uses the joint log-moment-generating function rather than a product of marginal moments.

Given maps \(Q:X\to\mathbb S^m\), \(q:X\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(r:X\to\mathbb R\), a quadratically perturbed scalar chance constraint has the form \[\mathbb P\!\left\{\xi^\top Q(x)\xi+2q(x)^\top\xi+r(x)\leq0\right\}\geq1-\epsilon.\] Equivalently, with \(y=(\xi^\top,1)^\top\) and \[M(x)=\begin{pmatrix}Q(x)&q(x)\\q(x)^\top&r(x)\end{pmatrix},\] the random loss equals \(y^\top M(x)y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Matrix-Chance Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalarization of a positive-semidefinite chance constraint for diagonal random matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(x,\xi)=\operatorname{Diag}(g_1(x,\xi),\ldots,g_m(x,\xi))\). For every realization of \(\xi\), \(D(x,\xi)\succeq0\) if and only if \(g_i(x,\xi)\geq0\) for every \(i\). Therefore the diagonal matrix chance constraint admits the exact joint-scalar representation \[\mathbb P\{D(x,\xi)\succeq0\}\geq1-\epsilon\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathbb P\{g_i(x,\xi)\geq0\ \forall i\}\geq1-\epsilon.\] This is a joint chance constraint, not generally a collection of independent marginal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive semidefiniteness of a diagonal random matrix is exactly the simultaneous nonnegativity of all diagonal entries.
assumptions_latex: \(D(x,\xi)\) is real and diagonal almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{D(x,\xi)\succeq0\}=\mathbb P\{g_i(x,\xi)\geq0\ \forall i\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal PSD scalarization is mathematically standard, exact, and correctly identified as a joint chance event, and representation fits the leaf. knowledge_statements.title: Arrow Matrix-Chance Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement scalarization of an arrow-shaped positive-semidefinite chance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x,\xi)=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha(x,\xi)&b(x,\xi)^\top\\b(x,\xi)&\operatorname{Diag}(d(x,\xi))\end{pmatrix}\), and suppose \(d_i(x,\xi)>0\) almost surely. The Schur complement gives \[A(x,\xi)\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \alpha(x,\xi)-\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{b_i(x,\xi)^2}{d_i(x,\xi)}\geq0.\] Hence the matrix chance constraint is exactly the scalar chance constraint that the displayed Schur complement is nonnegative, under the strict positivity assumption on the diagonal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive diagonal block, an arrow-matrix PSD chance constraint is exactly a scalar Schur-complement chance constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(A(x,\xi)\) is real symmetric and arrow-shaped almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\{A(x,\xi)\succeq0\}=\mathbb P\{\alpha(x,\xi)\geq\sum_i b_i(x,\xi)^2/d_i(x,\xi)\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and define its dual by \[K^*=\{y\in E:\langle y,z\rangle\geq0\ \forall z\in K\}.\] Let \((\Omega,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, let \(\xi:\Omega\to\Xi\) be a random element, let \(X\) be a decision set, and let \(G:X\times\Xi\to E\) be measurable in its second argument. For \(0<\epsilon<1\), a conic chance constraint is \(\mathbb P\{G(x,\xi)\in K\}\geq1-\epsilon\). By finite-dimensional bipolarity, for every realization, \[G(x,\xi)\in K\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle y,G(x,\xi)\rangle\geq0\quad\forall y\in K^*.\] Thus the conic chance event is an exact joint family of scalar inequalities indexed by \(K^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone membership with high probability is pointwise equivalent to simultaneous nonnegativity of all dual-cone scalarizations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone, let \(G:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^m\) be affine, let \(\xi:\Omega\to\mathbb R^q\) be a measurable random vector, and let \(\varepsilon\in[0,1]\). knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Form Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-ball uncertainty in a scalar affine robust inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^q\), let \(\|\cdot\|_*\) be its dual norm, let \(\rho\ge0\), and set \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^q:\|u\|\le\rho\}\). For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(f(x,u)=\alpha(x)+\langle\beta(x),u\rangle\), where \(\alpha:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex and \(\beta:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) is affine. Then \[f(x,u)\le0\quad\text{for all }u\in U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\alpha(x)+\rho\|\beta(x)\|_*\le0.\] The deterministic right-hand inequality is convex in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar inequality affine in norm-ball uncertainty is robust exactly when its nominal term plus the radius times the dual norm of its uncertain coefficient is nonpositive.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Generated Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic-duality reformulation of a scalar affine robust inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*=\{y\in\mathbb R^p:\langle y,k\rangle\ge0\ \forall k\in K\}\), and let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^q:Fu+g\in K\}\), where \(F\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) and \(g\in\mathbb R^p\). Let \(\alpha:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(\beta:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\). If the conic support problem has zero duality gap and an attained dual optimum, then \[\alpha(x)+\beta(x)^\mathsf Tu\le0\quad\text{for all }u\in U\] holds if and only if there exists \(y\in K^*\) such that \[F^\mathsf Ty=-\beta(x),\qquad\alpha(x)+g^\mathsf Ty\le0.\] Equivalently, \[\sup_{u\in U}\beta(x)^\mathsf Tu=\min\{g^\mathsf Ty:F^\mathsf Ty=-\beta(x),\ y\in K^*\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong conic duality replaces universal quantification over the uncertainty set by a dual-cone multiplier satisfying a deterministic equality and inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is a closed convex cone.
The conic support problem has zero duality gap and an attained dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(x)+\beta(x)^\mathsf Tu\le0\ \forall u\in U\Longleftrightarrow\exists y\in K^*:F^\mathsf Ty=-\beta(x),\ \alpha(x)+g^\mathsf Ty\le0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^q\), and define \[R=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:f_i(x,u)\le0\text{ for all }u\in U,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] The set \(R\) has an exact lifted conic reformulation if there exist integers \(r,p\), a closed convex cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), matrices \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^p\) such that \[R=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^r,\ Ax+Bz+c\in K\}.\] Thus projection of the lifted conic feasible set onto the \(x\)-coordinates recovers exactly \(R\).

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Cutting-Plane Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-generation algorithm for finitely constrained master problems with exact separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(U_0\subset U\) finite and tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), iteration \(k\) solves \[x^k\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{c^\mathsf Tx:f_i(x,u)\le0,\ u\in U_k,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] A separation oracle computes \((i_k,u^k)\in\arg\max_{i,u\in U}f_i(x^k,u)\). If \(f_{i_k}(x^k,u^k)\le\tau\), output \(x^k\); otherwise set \(U_{k+1}=U_k\cup\{u^k\}\) and repeat. The output satisfies \(f_i(x^k,u)\le\tau\) for every \(i\) and \(u\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a finite-scenario master problem and add a worst-case violating scenario until no violation exceeds the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each master problem is solved globally.
The separation oracle returns a global maximizer.
The relevant maxima over \(U\) are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_{i_k}(x^k,u^k)\le\tau\Longrightarrow f_i(x^k,u)\le\tau\ \forall i,\forall u\in U\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case scenario generation for testing and strengthening a robust candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate \(x^k\), compute for each uncertain constraint \[v_i^k=\max_{u\in U}f_i(x^k,u),\qquad u_i^k\in\arg\max_{u\in U}f_i(x^k,u).\] If \(\max_i v_i^k\le\tau\), certify \(x^k\) as \(\tau\)-robust feasible. Otherwise choose any \(i\) with \(v_i^k>\tau\), return \(u_i^k\) as an adversarial scenario, and append the deterministic constraint \(f_i(x,u_i^k)\le0\) to the master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize every constraint violation at the current candidate; certify approximate robustness or add a maximizing adversarial scenario to the master problem.
assumptions_latex: Each maximum over \(U\) is attained and solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i v_i^k\le\tau\) certifies approximate feasibility; \(v_i^k>\tau\) supplies a violated scenario.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scenario-generation procedure is plausible and fits the algorithm leaf, but no citation supports the exact procedure, global-oracle assumptions, or certification claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Reformulation–Generation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reformulation for tractable constraints combined with scenario generation for the remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the uncertain constraints into \(I_R\) and \(I_G\). Replace every constraint in \(I_R\) by an exact deterministic conic reformulation. Initialize finite scenario sets \(U_i^0\subset U_i\) for \(i\in I_G\), solve the resulting master problem, and compute \(v_i^k=\max_{u\in U_i}f_i(x^k,u)\). If \(v_i^k\le\tau\) for all \(i\in I_G\), output \(x^k\); otherwise add a maximizer for each selected violated constraint and repeat. The output is exact on \(I_R\) and \(\tau\)-robust feasible on \(I_G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reformulate tractable robust constraints exactly, while enforcing the remaining constraints by iterative worst-case scenario generation.
assumptions_latex: Reformulations for indices in \(I_R\) are exact.
Worst-case subproblems for indices in \(I_G\) are solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\) is robust feasible on \(I_R\) and satisfies \(f_i(x^k,u)\le\tau\) for all \(i\in I_G\) and \(u\in U_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hybrid algorithm is plausible and properly scoped, but no source supports the exact partitioned reformulation-generation procedure and its output guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Worst-Case Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact worst-case oracle over a compact polyhedral uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^q:Au\le b\}\) be nonempty and compact. Let \(d:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\). Given \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), solve \[v(x)=\max_{u\in\mathbb R^q}\{d(x)+c(x)^\mathsf Tu:Au\le b\}.\] Return an optimizer \(u^*\in U\) and the value \(v(x)\). For the robust inequality \(d(x)+c(x)^\mathsf Tu\le0\) for all \(u\in U\), the oracle certifies feasibility when \(v(x)\le0\), while \(u^*\) is a violation witness when \(v(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear worst-case oracle solves an LP over a compact polyhedral uncertainty set and returns either a robust-feasibility certificate or a violating scenario.
assumptions_latex: \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^q:Au\le b\}\) is nonempty and compact.
The oracle solves the linear program globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(x)\le0\Longleftrightarrow d(x)+c(x)^\mathsf Tu\le0\ \forall u\in U\); \(v(x)>0\Longrightarrow u^*\) violates the constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Worst-Case Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case linear optimization over a conically represented uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*=\{y\in\mathbb R^p:\langle y,k\rangle\ge0\ \forall k\in K\}\), let \(F\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^p\), and define \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^q:Fu+g\in K\}\). Let \(\alpha:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(\beta:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\). Given \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), solve \[v(x)=\max_{u\in\mathbb R^q}\{\alpha(x)+\beta(x)^\mathsf Tu:Fu+g\in K\}.\] Return a maximizing \(u^*\), and, when strong duality and dual attainment hold, a dual optimizer \(y^*\in K^*\) satisfying \[F^\mathsf Ty^*=-\beta(x),\qquad v(x)=\alpha(x)+g^\mathsf Ty^*.\] Then \(v(x)\le0\) certifies robust feasibility, whereas \(v(x)>0\) makes \(u^*\) a violation witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic oracle maximizes the uncertain affine constraint and may return matching primal and dual solutions certifying its worst-case value.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is nonempty and the maximum is attained.
Strong conic duality and dual attainment hold when a dual certificate is returned.
The primal conic problem is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(x)\le0\) certifies robustness, while \(v(x)>0\) makes \(u^*\) a violating scenario.

notation.meaning: dual cone under the nonnegative-pairing convention

knowledge_statements.title: Global Nonconvex Worst-Case Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified global maximization oracle for a nonconvex worst-case subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\), compact \(U\), tolerance \(\delta\ge0\), and possibly nonconcave \(u\mapsto f(x,u)\), maintain a feasible incumbent \(u^L\) with value \(L=f(x,u^L)\) and a valid global upper bound \(B\ge\max_{u\in U}f(x,u)\). Refine a global-optimization partition until \(B-L\le\delta\). Return \((u^L,L,B)\). If \(B\le0\), robust feasibility is certified; if \(L>0\), \(u^L\) certifies violation; otherwise the oracle is inconclusive at tolerance \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global nonconvex oracle returns a feasible adversary and a valid upper bound, enabling feasibility, violation, or tolerance-limited inconclusive status.
assumptions_latex: All regional upper bounds are globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\le0\) certifies robustness; \(L>0\) certifies violation; \(L\le0<B\) is inconclusive.

notation.meaning: incumbent feasible lower bound on the maximum
valid global upper bound on the maximum

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Robust-Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic dual multipliers certifying affine robust inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{p_i}\) be a closed convex cone with dual \(K_i^*=\{y\in\mathbb R^{p_i}:\langle y,k\rangle\ge0\ \forall k\in K_i\}\), let \(F_i\in\mathbb R^{p_i\times q_i}\), \(g_i\in\mathbb R^{p_i}\), and define \(U_i=\{u\in\mathbb R^{q_i}:F_i u+g_i\in K_i\}\). Let \(\alpha_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(\beta_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{q_i}\). Under strong conic duality and dual attainment, vectors \(y_i\in K_i^*\) satisfying \[F_i^\mathsf Ty_i=-\beta_i(x),\qquad\alpha_i(x)+g_i^\mathsf Ty_i\le0\] form a robust-feasibility certificate for \(\alpha_i(x)+\beta_i(x)^\mathsf Tu\le0\) for every \(u\in U_i\) and every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong conic duality, dual-cone multipliers satisfying finite equalities and inequalities certify that all uncertain affine constraints have nonpositive worst-case values.
assumptions_latex: Strong conic duality holds for each support problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y_i\}_{i=1}^m\) satisfying the displayed system certifies \(\alpha_i(x)+\beta_i(x)^\mathsf Tu\le0\) for all \(u\in U_i\) and all \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Violation Witnesses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct scenario certificate that a proposed decision is not robust feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{q_i}\) and \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{q_i}\to\mathbb R\). Consider the robust system \(f_i(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U_i\) and every \(i\). An adversarial violation witness for a candidate \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) is a pair \((i,\bar u)\) such that \(\bar u\in U_i\) and \[f_i(\bar x,\bar u)>0.\] These two conditions imply that \(\bar x\) is not robust feasible. For any specified \(\tau\ge0\), the stronger inequality \(f_i(\bar x,\bar u)>\tau\) also disproves \(\tau\)-robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One admissible scenario producing a positive constraint value is a finite, directly checkable certificate that the candidate is not robust feasible.
assumptions_latex: The value \(f_i(\bar x,\bar u)\) can be evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_i(\bar x,\bar u)>0\Longrightarrow\bar x\) is not robust feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Safe-Approximation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for an inner approximation of a robust feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,r\in\mathbb N\), let \(X\) and \(Z\) be sets, and, for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(U_i\) be an uncertainty set and \(f_i:X\times U_i\to\mathbb R\). Define \(F=\{x\in X:f_i(x,u)\le0\ \forall u\in U_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Let \(g_j:X\times Z\to\mathbb R\), \(j=1,\ldots,r\), define the tractable set \(\widehat F=\{x\in X:\exists z\in Z,\ g_j(x,z)\le0\ \forall j\}\), and suppose the inclusion \(\widehat F\subseteq F\) has been validated. For \(\bar x\in X\), any \(\bar z\in Z\) satisfying \(g_j(\bar x,\bar z)\le0\) for every \(j\), together with the validated inclusion, is a safe-approximation certificate of robust feasibility of \(\bar x\). Failure to find such a \(\bar z\) does not certify robust infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible auxiliary point for a validated inner approximation certifies robust feasibility; failure of that approximation need not imply true robust infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(m,r\in\mathbb N\), \(f_i:X\times U_i\to\mathbb R\), and \(g_j:X\times Z\to\mathbb R\).
The inclusion \(\widehat F\subseteq F\) has been validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_j(\bar x,\bar z)\le0\ \forall j\Longrightarrow \bar x\in F\).

notation.meaning: tractable inner approximation of the robust feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic Farkas certificate for an exact conic robust counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume an exact reformulation of the robust system is \(Az=b\), \(z\in K\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone with dual cone \(K^*\). Any \(y\in\mathbb R^p\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) is a robust infeasibility certificate: it certifies that the conic system, and hence the original robust system under the exact reformulation, is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an exact conic robust counterpart, a dual-cone vector whose pairing with the right-hand side is negative certifies robust infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
The conic formulation is equivalent to the original robust system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*,\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\Longrightarrow\{z\in K:Az=b\}=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Programming Robust Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP interface obtained by dualizing polyhedral uncertainty row by row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(a_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), \(b_0\in\mathbb R\), \(q\in\mathbb R^k\), and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:Du\le d\}\), where \(D\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times k}\), \(d\in\mathbb R^\ell\), and \(U\ne\varnothing\). Consider \((a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b_0+q^{\mathsf T}u\) for every \(u\in U\). If the associated support-function maximum is finite, linear-programming duality gives the equivalent representation
\[\exists\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^\ell:\quad D^{\mathsf T}\lambda=P^{\mathsf T}x-q,\qquad d^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le b_0-a_0^{\mathsf T}x.\]
Applying this construction to every uncertain affine row gives linear constraints in the original and dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust affine inequality over a nonempty polyhedron becomes linear constraints by introducing nonnegative variables dual to the uncertainty-set inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:Du\le d\}\ne\varnothing\), with \(D\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times k}\) and \(d\in\mathbb R^\ell\).
The support-function maximum in direction \(P^{\mathsf T}x-q\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in U}(P^{\mathsf T}x-q)^{\mathsf T}u\le b_0-a_0^{\mathsf T}x\) is equivalent to the displayed LP system.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Robust Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SOC representation for Euclidean-ball affine uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(a_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), \(b_0\in\mathbb R\), \(q\in\mathbb R^k\), and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:\|u\|_2\le\rho\}\), where \(\rho\ge0\). The robust affine inequality
\[(a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b_0+q^{\mathsf T}u\qquad\forall u\in U\]
is equivalent to
\[a_0^{\mathsf T}x-b_0+\rho\|P^{\mathsf T}x-q\|_2\le0.\]
Equivalently, there exists \(t\in\mathbb R\) such that \(\|P^{\mathsf T}x-q\|_2\le t\) and \(a_0^{\mathsf T}x-b_0+\rho t\le0\), yielding one second-order-cone constraint and one linear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing affine uncertainty over a Euclidean ball produces a norm term and an exact second-order-cone robust counterpart.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the Euclidean ball of radius \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall u\in U:\ (a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b_0+q^{\mathsf T}u\iff a_0^{\mathsf T}x-b_0+\rho\|P^{\mathsf T}x-q\|_2\le0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Robust Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: S-lemma SDP interface for one ellipsoidal quadratic uncertainty constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\succ0\), \(U=\{u:u^{\mathsf T}Qu\le1\}\), and \(q_x(u)=u^{\mathsf T}H(x)u+2h(x)^{\mathsf T}u+\alpha(x)\), with \(H,h,\alpha\) affine in \(x\). The robust inequality \(q_x(u)\le0\) for all \(u\in U\) is equivalent, by the lossless S-lemma, to the existence of \(\tau\ge0\) such that
\[\begin{pmatrix}H(x)-\tau Q&h(x)\\h(x)^{\mathsf T}&\alpha(x)+\tau\end{pmatrix}\preceq0.\]
Thus \(\tau\) and this linear matrix inequality form a semidefinite solver interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The S-lemma converts a quadratic inequality robust over one ellipsoid into an equivalent linear matrix inequality with one nonnegative multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succ0\), so the ellipsoid has a strict interior point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_x(u)\le0\ \forall u\in U\iff\exists\tau\ge0:\begin{pmatrix}H(x)-\tau Q&h(x)\\h(x)^{\mathsf T}&\alpha(x)+\tau\end{pmatrix}\preceq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed S-lemma sign convention is plausible and the representation fits the leaf, but an inspectable source for the lossless equivalence is required. Matrix dimensions should also be made explicit when sourced.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Based Robust Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane interface using adversarial maximization and separation oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given convex functions \(f_i(\cdot,u)\), compact sets \(U_i\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), initialize a relaxation with finitely many scenarios. At iterate \(x^k\), an adversarial oracle returns \(u_i^k\in\arg\max_{u\in U_i}f_i(x^k,u)\). If every \(f_i(x^k,u_i^k)\le\varepsilon\), stop and output \(x^k\). Otherwise, for each violated row choose \(s_i^k\in\partial_x f_i(x^k,u_i^k)\), add the valid cut
\[f_i(x^k,u_i^k)+(s_i^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^k)\le0,\]
and resolve the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adversarial oracle either certifies tolerance-feasibility or supplies a worst-case scenario whose subgradient defines a valid cut for the next relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Each \(U_i\) is compact and each adversarial maximum is attained.
Each \(f_i(\cdot,u)\) is convex and a subgradient oracle is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{u\in U_i}f_i(x^k,u)\le\varepsilon\ \forall i\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-robust feasibility; otherwise the displayed cut is valid.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The worst-case oracle and subgradient relaxation cut are mathematically plausible and algorithm is the correct kind, but no citation supports the algorithm, cut-generation interpretation, or stopping certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Undersized Uncertainty Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of safety when the modeled uncertainty set omits realizable parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scalar robust constraint \(ux\le1\) with \(x\ge0\), define \(F(U)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+:ux\le1\ \forall u\in U\}\). If \(U_M\subsetneq U_T\), membership in \(F(U_M)\) need not imply membership in \(F(U_T)\). For any \(\delta>0\), take \(U_M=[0,1]\) and \(U_T=[0,1+\delta]\). Then \(x=1\) belongs to \(F(U_M)\), but the realizable value \(u=1+\delta\) gives violation \(ux-1=\delta\), so \(x=1\notin F(U_T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model set smaller than the realizable set can certify a decision that fails under an omitted uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=1\in F(U_M)\) but \(x=1\notin F(U_T)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Uncertainty Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective conservatism caused by protecting against unrealizable parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(U_T\subsetneq U_M\), then the modeled robust feasible set satisfies \(F(U_M)\subseteq F(U_T)\), so safety is retained but attainable objective value may worsen. For \(\delta>0\), minimize \(-x\) subject to \(x\ge0\) and \(ux\le1\) for all \(u\) in the chosen set. With \(U_T=[0,1]\), the optimizer is \(x_T^*=1\); with \(U_M=[0,1+\delta]\), it is \(x_M^*=1/(1+\delta)\). The oversized model therefore incurs objective gap \(\delta/(1+\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging the uncertainty set preserves safety but can exclude useful decisions and strictly degrade the robust objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(U_M)\subseteq F(U_T)\) and, in the example, \(x_M^*=1/(1+\delta)<x_T^*=1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Geometry Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsafe support-function error from using an incorrectly oriented uncertainty geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the robust inequality \(u^{\mathsf T}x\le1\), define \(F(U)=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:u^{\mathsf T}x\le1\ \forall u\in U\}\). Let \(U_M=\{u\in\mathbb R^2:u_1^2/4+u_2^2\le1\}\) and \(U_T=\{u\in\mathbb R^2:u_1^2+u_2^2/4\le1\}\). These ellipsoids have equal area but different orientations and are not nested. For \(x=(0,1)\), \(\sup_{u\in U_M}u^{\mathsf T}x=1\), whereas \(\sup_{u\in U_T}u^{\mathsf T}x=2\). Thus matching a scalar size measure while misrepresenting uncertainty geometry can turn modeled feasibility into true violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncertainty sets of equal size can have different directional support, so the wrong geometry may certify a decision that violates the true robust constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(U_M\) and \(U_T\) are the displayed ellipsoids in \(\mathbb R^2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Ignored Dependence Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservatism caused by replacing coupled uncertainty with independent coordinate ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scalar decision \(x\in\mathbb R\), define \(F(U)=\{x\in\mathbb R:(u_1-u_2)x\le1\ \forall (u_1,u_2)\in U\}\). Let \(U_T=\{(u_1,u_2)\in\mathbb R^2:0\le u_1=u_2\le1\}\), but let the model ignore dependence and use \(U_M=[0,1]^2\). The true worst-case left side is \(0\) for every \(x\), whereas the modeled worst-case left side is \(|x|\). Consequently \(F(U_T)=\mathbb R\) while \(F(U_M)=[-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing coupled uncertainty by the product of its marginal ranges can create impossible joint scenarios and strictly shrink the robust feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(U_T)=\mathbb R\) while \(F(U_M)=[-1,1]\).

notation.meaning: feasible set for the uncertain scalar inequality over U

knowledge_statements.title: Static-Policy Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict feasibility loss from forbidding decisions that adapt to observed uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a two-stage robust model, let \(u\in[-1,1]\) be observed before choosing the recourse value \(y\), and impose \(y(u)\ge u\) and \(y(u)\le u\) for every \(u\). The adjustable policy \(y(u)=u\) is feasible. No static policy \(y(u)\equiv y_0\) is feasible, because it would require the same \(y_0\) to equal every \(u\in[-1,1]\). Thus restricting an adjustable decision rule to a constant can make a feasible adjustable robust problem infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant recourse decision may be infeasible even when a policy depending on observed uncertainty satisfies every scenario exactly.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty \(u\) is observed before recourse is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists y(\cdot)\ \forall u:\ y(u)=u\), but \(\nexists y_0\ \forall u:\ y_0=u\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructed example correctly demonstrates strict loss from restricting adjustable recourse to a static policy, and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Wise Protection Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Double counting caused by separately protecting components of a coupled uncertainty budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^2:u_1+u_2\le1\}\). The coupled robust inequality \(u_1+u_2\le1\) holds for every \(u\in U\). A row-wise epigraph approximation introduces constants \(t_i\) satisfying \(t_i\ge u_i\) for all \(u\in U\) and then requires \(t_1+t_2\le1\). Separate protection forces \(t_1\ge1\) and \(t_2\ge1\), so the approximation is infeasible. It combines worst cases attained at different scenarios and is therefore strictly conservative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Protecting coupled components separately can add mutually incompatible worst cases, making a valid coupled robust constraint appear infeasible.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty coordinates share the budget \(u_1+u_2\le1\).
Each epigraph variable is protected independently over the full set \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in U}(u_1+u_2)=1\), but \(\sup_{u\in U}u_1+\sup_{u\in U}u_2=2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example demonstrates conservatism from separately maximizing additive components within one constraint. It does not demonstrate row-wise protection conservatism: separate robustification of conjunctive constraint rows over the same uncertainty set is ordinarily exact. knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation-Induced Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservatism caused by replacing an exact robust constraint with a merely sufficient finite reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let each \(U_i\) be nonempty, and let \(f_i:X\times U_i\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Define \[F=\{x\in X:f_i(x,u)\leq0\text{ for every }u\in U_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] For \(p,k\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(G:X\times\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^k\), interpret \(G(x,z)\leq0\) componentwise, and define \[\widehat F=\{x\in X:\text{there exists }z\in\mathbb{R}^p\text{ such that }G(x,z)\leq0\}.\] If \(G(x,z)\leq0\) implies all original robust inequalities, then \(\widehat F\subseteq F\). Reformulation-induced conservatism means \(\widehat F\subsetneq F\); the reformulation is exact precisely when \(\widehat F=F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficient finite reformulation is conservative when its projected feasible set is a strict subset of the exact robust feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(G(x,z)\leq0\) is sufficient for all original robust inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat F\subseteq F\), with conservatism exactly when \(\widehat F\subsetneq F\).

knowledge_statements.title: Safe-Approximation Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner approximation obtained from tractable upper bounds on worst-case constraint values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(U_i\neq\varnothing\), and let \(f_i:X\times U_i\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Define \[F=\{x\in X:v_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\qquad F_{\mathrm{safe}}=\{x\in X:\phi_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Then \(F_{\mathrm{safe}}\subseteq F\). Safe-approximation conservatism occurs precisely when \(F_{\mathrm{safe}}\subsetneq F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tractable upper bounds on the worst-case constraint values define a safe inner approximation, which is conservative when it excludes a robust-feasible decision.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Uncertainty Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of closure on continuous worst-case constraints and attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(\varnothing\neq U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\), and let \(f:X\times\overline U\to\mathbb{R}\) be such that \(f(x,\cdot)\) is continuous on \(\overline U\) for every \(x\in X\). Then, for every \(x\in X\), \[\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)=\sup_{u\in\overline U}f(x,u),\] and \[f(x,u)\leq0\text{ for every }u\in U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x,u)\leq0\text{ for every }u\in\overline U.\] Thus closure preserves the robust feasible set. If the supremum is attained over \(\overline U\) only at points outside \(U\), the same value is not attained over \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For continuous uncertainty dependence, closing the uncertainty set preserves robust feasibility and supremum values, although the original set may lack a maximizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Concavity of \(f(x,\cdot)\) permits its worst-case maximization over a convex set to be posed as convex optimization. knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Quadratic Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of generic exact scalar-multiplier reformulation with multiple quadratic uncertainty constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set and let \(q_0:X\times\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}\) be quadratic in its second argument. For quadratic functions \(q_j:\mathbb{R}^q\to\mathbb{R}\), define \[U=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^q:q_j(u)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] A sufficient certificate for \(q_0(x,u)\leq0\) for every \(u\in U\) is the existence of multipliers \(\lambda_j\geq0\) such that \[q_0(x,u)-\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jq_j(u)\leq0\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb{R}^q.\] For \(m=1\), under the scalar S-lemma hypotheses including existence of \(\bar u\) with \(q_1(\bar u)<0\), this certificate is necessary as well as sufficient. For \(m\geq2\), the analogous scalar-multiplier certificate is generally sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar S-lemma is exact for one quadratic uncertainty constraint under its regularity hypotheses, whereas multiple quadratic constraints generally provide only a safe multiplier certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a decision set, \(q_0(x,\cdot)\) is quadratic for every \(x\in X\), and each \(q_j\) is quadratic.
For the asserted one-constraint exactness, \(m=1\) and there exists \(\bar u\in\mathbb{R}^q\) with \(q_1(\bar u)<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nonnegative scalar-multiplier certificate is safe; it is exact in the one-constraint S-lemma setting but is not generally necessary when \(m\geq2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Uncertainty Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scenario expansion for explicitly listed finite uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(U=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\) be an explicitly enumerated finite uncertainty set, and let \(f:X\times U\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\). Then, for every \(x\in X\), \[f(x,u)\leq0\text{ for every }u\in U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x,u^k)\leq0,\ k=1,\ldots,N.\] The direct representation uses \(N\) constraint evaluations per robust constraint. This does not imply polynomial complexity for an implicitly represented discrete set, whose number of scenarios may be exponential in its input description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicitly listed finite uncertainty set admits exact scenario enumeration, whereas an implicitly represented discrete set may contain exponentially many scenarios.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Uncertainty Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function representation exposing the combinatorial separation problem inside a robust affine constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision set, let \(\varnothing\neq U\subseteq\{0,1\}^q\) be specified by combinatorial feasibility constraints, and let \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}^q\) and \(b:X\to\mathbb{R}\). For every \(x\in X\), \[c(x)^{\mathsf T}u\leq b(x)\text{ for every }u\in U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sigma_U(c(x))=\max_{u\in U}c(x)^{\mathsf T}u\leq b(x).\] Thus violation evaluation and separation require solving the combinatorial optimization problem encoded by \(U\). This representation yields polynomial-time separation only when the corresponding support-function problem is polynomially solvable or has a suitable tractable formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonempty finite combinatorial uncertainty, robust separation is support-function optimization over the discrete structure, so tractability depends on the underlying combinatorial problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a decision set and \(\varnothing\neq U\subseteq\{0,1\}^q\) is specified by combinatorial constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust separation is exactly the combinatorial optimization problem defining \(\sigma_U(c(x))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Complexity Escalation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary induced by implicitly represented discrete uncertainty sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), let \(U\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\) have a polynomial-size implicit description, and let \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(a_0\in\mathbb Q^n\), \(b\in\mathbb Q\), and \(x\in\mathbb Q^n\). Define \(h_U(c)=\max_{u\in U}c^{\mathsf T}u\). Exact evaluation of the robust residual \(a_0^{\mathsf T}x+h_U(Ax)-b\) is NP-hard whenever instances of an NP-hard linear-optimization problem over \(U\) can be encoded polynomially through coefficient vectors \(Ax\). If, additionally, the violation problem \(h_U(Ax)>b-a_0^{\mathsf T}x\) is NP-hard under a polynomial encoding of coefficients and thresholds, then deciding robust feasibility \(h_U(Ax)\le b-a_0^{\mathsf T}x\) is coNP-hard. Thus a compact nominal convex formulation need not yield a polynomial-time robust counterpart without a tractable optimization oracle or extended formulation for \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Computing the worst-case value over a compactly represented discrete uncertainty set can be NP-hard; when finding a violating uncertainty realization is NP-hard, the corresponding universal robust-feasibility decision is coNP-hard.
assumptions_latex: Instances and coefficient vectors \(Ax\) are related by a polynomial-time encoding.
For the decision claim, coefficients and thresholds are polynomially encodable and the associated violation problem is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{exact worst-case evaluation is NP-hard, and the stated feasibility decision is coNP-hard}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic-duality boundary for a robust counterpart after exact reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal Y\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(K\subseteq\mathcal X\) be a closed convex cone, let \(A:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\) be linear, and let \(c\in\mathcal X\) and \(b\in\mathcal Y\). Suppose an exact robust counterpart has primal value \(p^*=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and dual value \(d^*=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:c-A^*y\in K^*\}\). Weak duality gives \(d^*\le p^*\). When both values are finite, a robust duality gap is the failure condition \(d^*<p^*\), under which dual bounds cannot certify the robust optimum exactly. Such a gap can occur in the absence of regularity conditions that guarantee strong conic duality, including appropriate primal or dual Slater conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust duality gap occurs when an exact finite-dimensional conic robust counterpart and its dual have finite values with the dual value strictly below the primal value.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal Y\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
\(K\subseteq\mathcal X\) is a closed convex cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Infeasibility Interfaces

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb S_+^2\) and \(L=\{X(t):t\in\mathbb R\}\), where \(X(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&t\end{pmatrix}\). No member of \(L\) belongs to \(K\). knowledge_statements.title: Poor Uncertainty Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary for ellipsoidal uncertainty represented by anisotropic coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular, and define \(U_D=\{u\in\mathbb R^m:\|D^{-1}u\|_2\le1\}\). For every \(a\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\sup_{u\in U_D}a^{\mathsf T}u=\|D^{\mathsf T}a\|_2\). The coordinate map \(v\mapsto Dv\) has maximum Euclidean gain \(\sigma_{\max}(D)\), minimum gain \(\sigma_{\min}(D)\), and gain ratio \(\kappa_2(D)=\sigma_{\max}(D)/\sigma_{\min}(D)\). The representation enters a poor-scaling regime as \(\kappa_2(D)\) becomes large or unbounded, although the uncertainty set and its robust counterpart remain convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ellipsoidal uncertainty representation is poorly scaled when its shape matrix has a large ratio between maximum and minimum directional gains, even though convexity is preserved.
assumptions_latex: All norms and conditioning quantities are Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{u\in U_D}a^{\mathsf T}u=\|D^{\mathsf T}a\|_2\quad\text{and}\quad\kappa_2(D)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(D)}{\sigma_{\min}(D)}\)
