knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Counterpart Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of strict robust feasibility and positive feasibility margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For robust inequalities \(f_i(x,u)\le0\) over \(u\in U_i\), define \(g_i(x)=\sup_{u\in U_i}f_i(x,u)\) and the strict-feasibility margin \(\rho=\sup_x\min_i[-g_i(x)]\). If the robust feasible set is nonempty but \(\rho=0\), the counterpart has no strictly feasible point and lies on the degeneracy boundary. This boundary can be perturbationally fragile: the one-dimensional convex family \(g_\varepsilon(x)=x^2+\varepsilon\) has feasible set \(\{0\}\) at \(\varepsilon=0\), whereas every \(\varepsilon>0\) makes \(g_\varepsilon(x)\le0\) infeasible. Thus arbitrarily small right-hand-side tightening can destroy feasibility at zero margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust counterpart is geometrically degenerate when feasible but lacking strict margin; an arbitrarily small tightening may then eliminate feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) is a proper convex worst-case function.
The supremum defining each \(g_i\) is well-defined.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-enumeration size for finitely supported uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision space, let \(r,N\in\mathbb N\), let \(U=\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\), and let \(f_i:X\times U\to\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,\ldots,r\). The robust system \(f_i(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U\) is exactly equivalent to the \(rN\) scalar inequalities \(f_i(x,u^j)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,r\) and \(j=1,\ldots,N\). If one instance requires at most \(T\) arithmetic operations and \(S\) storage words, full enumeration requires \(O(rNT)\) operations and \(O(rNS)\) storage. If the same scenario family has a compact description of length \(q\) with \(N=2^{\Omega(q)}\), then the enumerated counterpart is exponentially large in \(q\), absent structure-based compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerating N scenarios for r robust constraints creates rN scalar constraints; this is exponential relative to a compact encoding of length q when N grows exponentially in q.
assumptions_latex: Each scenario-constraint instance has arithmetic cost at most \(T\) and storage cost at most \(S\).
For the exponential-size conclusion, the scenario family has a compact description of length \(q\) and \(N=2^{\Omega(q)}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{constraint count}=rN,\quad\text{evaluation cost}=O(rNT),\quad\text{storage}=O(rNS)\)

notation.meaning: Length of a separate compact description of the scenario family.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Worst-Case Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision ambiguity caused by additive error in worst-case evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(x)=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\), so robust feasibility requires \(\phi(x)\le0\). Suppose an oracle returns \(\widehat u\in U\) with \(f(x,\widehat u)\ge\phi(x)-\varepsilon\), and set \(\widehat\phi(x)=f(x,\widehat u)\). Then \(\widehat\phi(x)\le\phi(x)\le\widehat\phi(x)+\varepsilon\). Hence \(\widehat\phi(x)>0\) certifies violation, while \(\widehat\phi(x)+\varepsilon\le0\) certifies feasibility. If \(-\varepsilon<\widehat\phi(x)\le0\), neither conclusion follows: the oracle may report a nonpositive sampled value although the exact worst-case value is positive. This width-\(\varepsilon\) band is the instability interface for additive-error worst-case oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive-error worst-case oracle cannot reliably classify points whose estimated robust residual lies within epsilon of the feasibility boundary.
assumptions_latex: The oracle has certified additive accuracy \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\varepsilon<\widehat\phi(x)\le0\) is an indeterminate feasibility band

notation.meaning: Value returned by the worst-case oracle.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-error inequalities and indeterminate band are mathematically consistent and fit the failure-boundary leaf, but the record has no citation. An authoritative source and explicit domains for x, U, and f are required.
